ko.title: 165,000개의 일자리와 4.1%의 실업률: 강력한 10월 고용 보고서가 모두에게 좋은 소식이 아닌 이유

segments.src: A monthly jobs report is often summed up in a single headline number.
segments.tr: 월간 고용 보고서는 종종 하나의 헤드라인 수치로 요약됩니다.

segments.src: For October, that number was 165,000 jobs added, with the unemployment rate at 4.1%.
segments.tr: 10월의 경우, 그 수치는 165,000개의 일자리 증가였으며 실업률은 4.1%였습니다.

segments.src: Payrolls came in above what forecasters expected, and on the surface that looks like good news.
segments.tr: 고용 수치는 예측치를 상회했으며, 표면적으로는 좋은 소식처럼 보입니다.

segments.src: Look closer and the picture is more mixed.
segments.tr: 더 자세히 들여다보면 상황은 더 복합적입니다.

segments.src: Hiring was uneven across industries and age groups, and financial markets tend to treat a strong labor market as a reason to expect higher borrowing costs for longer.
segments.tr: 산업별, 연령대별로 고용 상황은 불균형했으며, 금융 시장은 강력한 노동 시장을 더 높은 차입 비용이 더 오래 지속될 것이라는 신호로 해석하는 경향이 있습니다.

segments.src: This article walks through what the figures suggest, why strength for the economy and relief for households and investors are not always the same thing, and which details are worth watching in the months ahead.
segments.tr: 이 기사에서는 이러한 수치가 무엇을 시사하는지, 경제의 강세와 가계 및 투자자의 안도가 왜 항상 같은 것은 아닌지, 그리고 앞으로 몇 달 동안 어떤 세부 사항을 주목해야 하는지 살펴봅니다.

segments.src: *This article is for general information only.
segments.tr: *이 기사는 일반적인 정보 제공만을 목적으로 합니다.

segments.src: It is not financial, investment, or employment advice.*
segments.tr: 금융, 투자 또는 고용에 대한 조언이 아닙니다.*

segments.src: ## What the headline numbers say
segments.tr: ## 헤드라인 수치가 의미하는 것

segments.src: The monthly employment report comes from two separate surveys.
segments.tr: 월간 고용 보고서는 두 가지 별도의 조사에서 나옵니다.

segments.src: One asks employers how many people are on their payrolls.
segments.tr: 하나는 고용주에게 급여 명부에 몇 명의 직원이 있는지 묻는 조사입니다.

segments.src: The other asks households whether they are working or looking for work.
segments.tr: 다른 하나는 가구에 일하고 있는지 또는 일자리를 찾고 있는지 묻는 조사입니다.

segments.src: The 165,000 figure comes from the employer survey.
segments.tr: 165,000명이라는 수치는 고용주 조사에서 나온 것입니다.

segments.src: The 4.1% unemployment rate comes from the household survey.
segments.tr: 4.1%의 실업률은 가구 조사에서 나온 것입니다.

segments.src: A few points of context help:
segments.tr: 몇 가지 맥락을 이해하면 도움이 됩니다:

segments.src: - **165,000 is solid, not spectacular.** In a growing economy, a gain in this range is generally enough to absorb new entrants to the labor force. It is not the kind of surge that signals overheating on its own.
segments.tr: - **165,000명은 견고하지만, 놀라운 수준은 아닙니다.** 성장하는 경제에서 이 정도 범위의 증가는 일반적으로 노동 시장에 새로 진입하는 인력을 흡수하기에 충분합니다. 이는 그 자체로 과열을 알리는 급증세는 아닙니다.

segments.src: - **4.1% is historically low.** By long-run standards, an unemployment rate near 4% is consistent with a tight labor market, where employers compete for workers.
segments.tr: - **4.1%는 역사적으로 낮은 수준입니다.** 장기적인 기준으로 볼 때, 4%에 가까운 실업률은 고용주들이 노동자를 구하기 위해 경쟁하는 타이트한 노동 시장과 일치합니다.

segments.src: - **Beating expectations matters in its own right.** Forecasters publish estimates before each report. A result above the consensus is treated as a surprise, and surprises move markets even when the underlying change is modest.
segments.tr: - **예상치를 뛰어넘는다는 것 자체가 중요합니다.** 예측가들은 각 보고서가 나오기 전에 추정치를 발표합니다. 컨센서스를 상회하는 결과는 놀라운 것으로 간주되며, 근본적인 변화가 완만하더라도 이러한 놀라움은 시장을 움직입니다.

segments.src: - **Numbers get revised.** Initial estimates are often adjusted in later months. One report is a snapshot, not a verdict.
segments.tr: - **수치는 수정됩니다.** 초기 추정치는 종종 나중에 수정됩니다. 하나의 보고서는 스냅샷일 뿐, 최종 판결이 아닙니다.

segments.src: ## Where hiring was strong, and where it wasn't
segments.tr: ## 고용이 강했던 곳과 그렇지 않았던 곳

segments.src: A headline total can hide very different experiences underneath.
segments.tr: 헤드라인 총계는 그 이면에 있는 매우 다른 경험들을 숨길 수 있습니다.

segments.src: In reports like this one, job gains tend to cluster in a small number of sectors, while others stay flat or shrink.
segments.tr: 이와 같은 보고서에서 일자리 증가는 소수의 부문에 집중되는 경향이 있는 반면, 다른 부문은 정체되거나 축소됩니다.

segments.src: **Industries.** Health care, social assistance, and government have been consistent sources of job growth in recent years, partly because demand for those services is steady and less sensitive to the business cycle.
segments.tr: **산업.** 의료, 사회 복지, 정부 부문은 최근 몇 년간 일자리 성장의 일관된 원천이었는데, 이는 부분적으로 해당 서비스에 대한 수요가 꾸준하고 경기 순환에 덜 민감하기 때문입니다.

segments.src: Sectors that depend more on discretionary spending or interest rates, such as parts of manufacturing, construction, retail, and information technology, have tended to be more volatile.
segments.tr: 제조업, 건설업, 소매업, 정보 기술의 일부와 같이 재량적 지출이나 금리에 더 의존하는 부문은 더 변동성이 큰 경향이 있었습니다.

segments.src: When most of the gains come from a few areas, a strong total can coexist with real weakness elsewhere.
segments.tr: 증가의 대부분이 소수의 분야에서 나올 때, 강력한 총계는 다른 곳의 실질적인 약세와 공존할 수 있습니다.

segments.src: **Age groups.** Workers in their prime working years, roughly 25 to 54, have had very high employment rates.
segments.tr: **연령대.** 대략 25세에서 54세 사이의 핵심 근로 연령층은 매우 높은 고용률을 보였습니다.

segments.src: Younger workers and new graduates often face a harder search when employers slow hiring for entry-level roles.
segments.tr: 더 젊은 근로자와 신규 졸업생들은 고용주가 초급 역할에 대한 채용을 늦출 때 종종 더 어려운 구직 상황에 직면합니다.

segments.src: Older workers who lose a job may take longer to find a new one.
segments.tr: 일자리를 잃은 고령 근로자는 새로운 일자리를 찾는 데 더 오랜 시간이 걸릴 수 있습니다.

segments.src: The overall unemployment rate averages all of this out, which is why a good headline can feel out of step with what some job seekers report.
segments.tr: 전체 실업률은 이 모든 것을 평균화한 것이며, 이것이 바로 좋은 헤드라인이 일부 구직자들이 보고하는 상황과 동떨어져 느껴질 수 있는 이유입니다.

segments.src: **Hours and job quality.** The count of jobs does not show whether positions are full-time, part-time, or temporary.
segments.tr: **근로 시간 및 일자리 질.** 일자리 수는 해당 직위가 정규직인지, 시간제인지, 임시직인지 보여주지 않습니다.

segments.src: Analysts also look at average weekly hours and at the share of people working part-time who would prefer full-time work.
segments.tr: 분석가들은 또한 평균 주당 근로 시간과 정규직을 선호하지만 시간제로 일하는 사람들의 비율을 살펴봅니다.

segments.src: ## Wages: growing, but is it enough?
segments.tr: ## 임금: 성장하고 있지만, 충분한가?

segments.src: Pay is the second half of the story.
segments.tr: 급여는 이야기의 두 번째 절반입니다.

segments.src: When unemployment is low, employers usually have to offer more to attract and keep workers, so wage growth tends to stay firm.
segments.tr: 실업률이 낮을 때 고용주는 일반적으로 노동자를 유치하고 유지하기 위해 더 많은 급여를 제공해야 하므로 임금 상승률은 견고하게 유지되는 경향이 있습니다.

segments.src: That is good news for workers if pay rises faster than prices.
segments.tr: 물가보다 급여가 더 빨리 오른다면 이는 근로자에게 좋은 소식입니다.

segments.src: It is more complicated if inflation has also been running above the central bank's 2% goal.
segments.tr: 인플레이션이 중앙은행의 2% 목표치를 상회해 왔다면 상황은 더 복잡해집니다.

segments.src: In that case, solid wage growth can look like a risk to policymakers.
segments.tr: 그런 경우, 견고한 임금 상승은 정책 입안자들에게 위험으로 보일 수 있습니다.

segments.src: Their concern is that higher labor costs get passed on through prices, especially in service industries where labor is a large share of the bill.
segments.tr: 그들의 우려는 노동 비용 상승이 가격을 통해 전가되는 것인데, 특히 노동 비중이 큰 서비스 산업에서 그렇습니다.

segments.src: Averages also hide differences.
segments.tr: 평균은 또한 차이를 숨깁니다.

segments.src: Workers who change jobs have often received larger raises than those who stay put, while pay increases for people in the same role have been smaller.
segments.tr: 직장을 옮기는 근로자는 종종 제자리에 머무는 근로자보다 더 큰 인상률을 받았지만, 같은 역할에 있는 사람들의 급여 인상은 더 작았습니다.

segments.src: Households that carry high rent, mortgage, or credit card costs may still feel stretched even when the national wage figure looks healthy.
segments.tr: 높은 임대료, 주택 담보 대출 또는 신용 카드 비용을 부담하는 가계는 국가 임금 수치가 건강해 보일 때조차 여전히 경제적 압박을 느낄 수 있습니다.

segments.src: ## Job-switching: a sign of confidence, or a fading one
segments.tr: ## 이직: 자신감의 신호인가, 아니면 희미해지는 신호인가

segments.src: Economists watch how often workers quit voluntarily.
segments.tr: 경제학자들은 근로자가 자발적으로 퇴사하는 빈도를 지켜봅니다.

segments.src: People generally leave a job when they are confident they can find a better one.
segments.tr: 사람들은 일반적으로 더 나은 일자리를 찾을 수 있다고 확신할 때 직장을 떠납니다.

segments.src: A high quit rate suggests a confident labor market with plenty of openings.
segments.tr: 높은 퇴사율은 일자리가 많은 자신감 있는 노동 시장을 시사합니다.

segments.src: A falling quit rate suggests workers are staying put, and that employers are posting fewer openings.
segments.tr: 낮아지는 퇴사율은 근로자들이 현재 직장에 머물고 있으며, 고용주들이 더 적은 채용 공고를 내고 있음을 시사합니다.

segments.src: In the past few years, the pace of job-switching has cooled from its peak.
segments.tr: 지난 몇 년 동안 이직 속도는 정점에서 식었습니다.

segments.src: That has two effects:
segments.tr: 이는 두 가지 효과를 가져옵니다:

segments.src: - **Less pressure on pay.** When fewer people change jobs, employers feel less need to raise wages to compete.
segments.tr: - **임금에 대한 압박 감소.** 더 적은 사람들이 직장을 옮길 때, 고용주는 경쟁을 위해 임금을 인상해야 할 필요성을 덜 느낍니다.

segments.src: - **Harder entry for new job seekers.** Fewer vacancies are created when current employees stay in their roles, which can make it tougher for the unemployed and for people entering the workforce.
segments.tr: - **신규 구직자의 진입 장벽.** 현재 직원들이 자신의 역할을 유지하면 공석이 덜 생기며, 이는 실업자와 노동 시장에 진입하는 사람들에게 더 어려울 수 있습니다.

segments.src: This helps explain why a strong payroll number and a feeling of "a low-hire, low-fire" job market can both be true at once.
segments.tr: 이는 강력한 고용 수치와 "낮은 채용, 낮은 해고"의 노동 시장이라는 느낌이 동시에 사실일 수 있는 이유를 설명하는 데 도움이 됩니다.

segments.src: ## Why markets read good news as a rate risk
segments.tr: ## 시장이 좋은 소식을 금리 위험으로 읽는 이유

segments.src: For many people, the most puzzling part of a jobs report day is that stocks or bonds sometimes fall after good news.
segments.tr: 많은 사람들에게 고용 보고서 발표 날 가장 당혹스러운 부분은 좋은 소식 이후에 주식이나 채권이 때때로 하락한다는 것입니다.

segments.src: The reason is interest rates.
segments.tr: 그 이유는 금리 때문입니다.

segments.src: The Federal Reserve sets its policy rate with two goals in mind: maximum employment and stable prices.
segments.tr: 연방준비제도(Fed)는 최대 고용과 물가 안정이라는 두 가지 목표를 염두에 두고 정책 금리를 설정합니다.

segments.src: When the labor market is strong and wages are rising, the case for lowering rates weakens.
segments.tr: 노동 시장이 강하고 임금이 상승할 때 금리 인하의 근거는 약화됩니다.

segments.src: Investors who had been counting on rate cuts may have to change their expectations.
segments.tr: 금리 인하를 기대했던 투자자들은 기대를 수정해야 할 수도 있습니다.

segments.src: Here is how that chain usually works:
segments.tr: 그 연쇄 반응은 보통 다음과 같이 작동합니다:

segments.src: 1. **A stronger-than-expected report** suggests the economy does not need extra support from lower rates.
segments.tr: 1. **예상보다 강력한 보고서**는 경제가 낮은 금리로 인한 추가 지원이 필요하지 않음을 시사합니다.

segments.src: 2. **Expectations for rate cuts are pushed back** or reduced.
segments.tr: 2. **금리 인하에 대한 기대가 뒤로 밀리거나** 줄어듭니다.

segments.src: 3. **Government bond yields often rise**, because investors now expect rates to stay higher for longer.
segments.tr: 3. **정부 채권 수익률은 종종 상승합니다.** 투자자들이 이제 금리가 더 오랫동안 높게 유지될 것으로 예상하기 때문입니다.

segments.src: 4. **Higher yields can weigh on stock prices**, particularly for companies that rely on borrowing or whose value depends heavily on future earnings.
segments.tr: 4. **더 높은 수익률은 주가에 부담을 줄 수 있습니다.** 특히 차입에 의존하거나 가치가 미래 수익에 크게 의존하는 기업의 경우 더욱 그렇습니다.

segments.src: 5. **Borrowing costs for households stay elevated.** Mortgage rates, auto loans, and credit cards tend to follow broader rate expectations.
segments.tr: 5. **가계의 차입 비용은 높은 수준을 유지합니다.** 주택 담보 대출, 자동차 대출, 신용 카드는 더 광범위한 금리 기대를 따르는 경향이 있습니다.

segments.src: This is why a report can be good for workers and still unwelcome for people hoping for cheaper loans.
segments.tr: 이것이 바로 보고서가 근로자에게는 좋을 수 있지만 더 저렴한 대출을 바라는 사람들에게는 여전히 환영받지 못하는 이유입니다.

segments.src: It also explains why traders often react more to the difference between actual and expected numbers than to the numbers themselves.
segments.tr: 또한 트레이더들이 종종 수치 자체보다 실제 수치와 예상 수치 간의 차이에 더 많이 반응하는 이유를 설명합니다.

segments.src: ## What to watch next
segments.tr: ## 다음에 주목할 것

segments.src: A single month rarely changes the broader direction.
segments.tr: 단 한 달의 수치가 더 넓은 방향을 바꾸는 경우는 드뭅니다.

segments.src: These indicators give a fuller view:
segments.tr: 다음 지표들은 더 완전한 시각을 제공합니다:

segments.src: - **Revisions to prior months**, which can change the story of how strong hiring really was.
segments.tr: - **이전 달에 대한 수정치.** 이는 고용이 실제로 얼마나 강력했는지에 대한 이야기를 바꿀 수 있습니다.

segments.src: - **Average hourly earnings**, to see whether wage growth is speeding up or slowing down.
segments.tr: - **평균 시간당 임금.** 임금 상승이 가속화되고 있는지 아니면 둔화되고 있는지 확인하기 위함입니다.

segments.src: - **The labor force participation rate**, which shows whether more people are coming back to look for work.
segments.tr: - **노동 참가율.** 더 많은 사람들이 일자리를 찾기 위해 돌아오고 있는지 보여줍니다.

segments.src: - **Job openings and quit rates**, from the monthly JOLTS survey, for a read on employer demand and worker confidence.
segments.tr: - **일자리 공석 및 퇴사율.** 월간 JOLTS 조사에서 고용주 수요와 근로자 자신감을 읽기 위함입니다.

segments.src: - **Weekly jobless claims**, an early signal of layoffs.
segments.tr: - **주간 실업 수당 청구 건수.** 해고의 초기 신호입니다.

segments.src: - **Inflation data and Federal Reserve communications**, since these shape how policymakers respond to the labor market.
segments.tr: - **인플레이션 데이터 및 연방준비제도 커뮤니케이션.** 이는 정책 입안자들이 노동 시장에 어떻게 대응할지를 결정하기 때문입니다.

segments.src: ## The bottom line
segments.tr: ## 결론

segments.src: A report showing 165,000 new jobs and a 4.1% unemployment rate is, by most measures, evidence of a resilient labor market.
segments.tr: 165,000개의 새로운 일자리와 4.1%의 실업률을 보여주는 보고서는 대부분의 지표에서 회복력 있는 노동 시장의 증거입니다.

segments.src: But resilience is not the same as broad-based strength.
segments.tr: 하지만 회복력이 광범위한 강세와 같은 것은 아닙니다.

segments.src: Gains concentrated in a few industries, uneven results across age groups, and slower job-switching all suggest that many people are not feeling the benefit equally.
segments.tr: 소수의 산업에 집중된 증가, 연령대별로 불균형한 결과, 그리고 더딘 이직은 모두 많은 사람들이 그 혜택을 동등하게 느끼지 못하고 있음을 시사합니다.

segments.src: And because strong employment can delay interest rate cuts, good news for the job market can mean a more cautious outlook for borrowers and investors.
segments.tr: 그리고 강력한 고용은 금리 인하를 지연시킬 수 있기 때문에, 고용 시장에 대한 좋은 소식은 차입자와 투자자에게는 더 신중한 전망을 의미할 수 있습니다.

segments.src: The most useful way to read a jobs report is to look past the headline: ask who is being hired, how much they are paid, and what it means for the path of interest rates.
segments.tr: 고용 보고서를 읽는 가장 유용한 방법은 헤드라인 너머를 보는 것입니다. 누가 고용되고 있는지, 그들이 얼마를 받는지, 그리고 그것이 금리 경로에 무엇을 의미하는지 질문하십시오.

segments.src: *Figures cited are as reported for October and may be revised.
segments.tr: *언급된 수치는 10월 기준으로 보고된 것이며 수정될 수 있습니다.

segments.src: Readers should consult official sources, such as the Bureau of Labor Statistics, for the latest data.

zh.title: 16.5万个就业岗位与4.1%的失业率：为何强劲的10月报告并非对所有人都是好消息

segments.src: A monthly jobs report is often summed up in a single headline number.
segments.tr: 每月发布的就业报告通常会用一个单一的头条数字来概括。

segments.src: For October, that number was 165,000 jobs added, with the unemployment rate at 4.1%.
segments.tr: 10月份，这个数字是新增16.5万个就业岗位，失业率为4.1%。

segments.src: Payrolls came in above what forecasters expected, and on the surface that looks like good news.
segments.tr: 就业人数高于预测者的预期，从表面上看，这似乎是个好消息。

segments.src: Look closer and the picture is more mixed.
segments.tr: 仔细观察，情况则更为复杂。

segments.src: Hiring was uneven across industries and age groups, and financial markets tend to treat a strong labor market as a reason to expect higher borrowing costs for longer.
segments.tr: 各行业和年龄组的招聘情况并不均衡，而且金融市场往往将强劲的劳动力市场视为预期借贷成本将在更长时间内保持高位的理由。

segments.src: This article walks through what the figures suggest, why strength for the economy and relief for households and investors are not always the same thing, and which details are worth watching in the months ahead.
segments.tr: 本文将梳理这些数据所暗示的内容，解释为什么经济强劲与家庭及投资者获得缓解并不总是同一回事，并指出未来几个月值得关注的细节。

segments.src: *This article is for general information only.
segments.tr: *本文仅供一般参考。

segments.src: It is not financial, investment, or employment advice.*
segments.tr: 它不构成财务、投资或就业建议。*

segments.src: ## What the headline numbers say
segments.tr: ## 头条数字说明了什么

segments.src: The monthly employment report comes from two separate surveys.
segments.tr: 每月的就业报告来自两项独立的调查。

segments.src: One asks employers how many people are on their payrolls.
segments.tr: 一项调查询问雇主其工资单上有多少人。

segments.src: The other asks households whether they are working or looking for work.
segments.tr: 另一项调查询问家庭成员是否正在工作或寻找工作。

segments.src: The 165,000 figure comes from the employer survey.
segments.tr: 16.5万这个数字来自雇主调查。

segments.src: The 4.1% unemployment rate comes from the household survey.
segments.tr: 4.1%的失业率来自家庭调查。

segments.src: A few points of context help:
segments.tr: 以下几点背景信息会有所帮助：

segments.src: - **165,000 is solid, not spectacular.** In a growing economy, a gain in this range is generally enough to absorb new entrants to the labor force. It is not the kind of surge that signals overheating on its own.
segments.tr: - **16.5万是一个稳健的数字，而非惊人。** 在增长型经济中，这一范围内的增长通常足以吸收劳动力市场的新进入者。这并不是那种本身就预示着过热的激增。

segments.src: - **4.1% is historically low.** By long-run standards, an unemployment rate near 4% is consistent with a tight labor market, where employers compete for workers.
segments.tr: - **4.1%处于历史低位。** 从长期标准来看，接近4%的失业率与紧张的劳动力市场相一致，在这种市场中，雇主需要竞争人才。

segments.src: - **Beating expectations matters in its own right.** Forecasters publish estimates before each report. A result above the consensus is treated as a surprise, and surprises move markets even when the underlying change is modest.
segments.tr: - **超出预期本身就很重要。** 预测者会在每份报告发布前公布估计值。高于共识的结果会被视为一种意外，即使潜在的变化幅度不大，意外也会推动市场波动。

segments.src: - **Numbers get revised.** Initial estimates are often adjusted in later months. One report is a snapshot, not a verdict.
segments.tr: - **数字会被修正。** 初始估计值往往会在随后的几个月中进行调整。一份报告只是一个快照，而不是最终定论。

segments.src: ## Where hiring was strong, and where it wasn't
segments.tr: ## 招聘强劲与疲软的领域

segments.src: A headline total can hide very different experiences underneath.
segments.tr: 头条总数可能会掩盖其下截然不同的实际情况。

segments.src: In reports like this one, job gains tend to cluster in a small number of sectors, while others stay flat or shrink.
segments.tr: 在像这样的报告中，就业增长往往集中在少数几个行业，而其他行业则保持平稳或萎缩。

segments.src: **Industries.** Health care, social assistance, and government have been consistent sources of job growth in recent years, partly because demand for those services is steady and less sensitive to the business cycle.
segments.tr: **行业。** 近年来，医疗保健、社会援助和政府部门一直是就业增长的稳定来源，部分原因是这些服务的需求稳定，且对商业周期的敏感度较低。

segments.src: Sectors that depend more on discretionary spending or interest rates, such as parts of manufacturing, construction, retail, and information technology, have tended to be more volatile.
segments.tr: 那些更依赖可自由支配支出或利率的行业，例如制造业、建筑业、零售业和信息技术的部分领域，往往波动性更大。

segments.src: When most of the gains come from a few areas, a strong total can coexist with real weakness elsewhere.
segments.tr: 当大部分增长来自少数几个领域时，强劲的总数可能与其它领域的真正疲软并存。

segments.src: **Age groups.** Workers in their prime working years, roughly 25 to 54, have had very high employment rates.
segments.tr: **年龄组。** 处于黄金工作年龄（大约25至54岁）的劳动者就业率一直非常高。

segments.src: Younger workers and new graduates often face a harder search when employers slow hiring for entry-level roles.
segments.tr: 当雇主放缓入门级职位的招聘时，年轻工人和应届毕业生往往面临更艰难的求职过程。

segments.src: Older workers who lose a job may take longer to find a new one.
segments.tr: 失业的年长工人可能需要更长时间才能找到新工作。

segments.src: The overall unemployment rate averages all of this out, which is why a good headline can feel out of step with what some job seekers report.
segments.tr: 整体失业率平均了所有这些情况，这就是为什么一个好的头条新闻可能会让人觉得与一些求职者的报告不符。

segments.src: **Hours and job quality.** The count of jobs does not show whether positions are full-time, part-time, or temporary.
segments.tr: **工时与工作质量。** 就业人数统计并未显示职位是全职、兼职还是临时工。

segments.src: Analysts also look at average weekly hours and at the share of people working part-time who would prefer full-time work.
segments.tr: 分析师还会查看平均每周工时，以及那些希望从事全职工作的兼职人员的比例。

segments.src: ## Wages: growing, but is it enough?
segments.tr: ## 工资：在增长，但足够吗？

segments.src: Pay is the second half of the story.
segments.tr: 薪酬是故事的另一半。

segments.src: When unemployment is low, employers usually have to offer more to attract and keep workers, so wage growth tends to stay firm.
segments.tr: 当失业率较低时，雇主通常必须提供更高的薪酬来吸引和留住员工，因此工资增长往往保持坚挺。

segments.src: That is good news for workers if pay rises faster than prices.
segments.tr: 如果薪酬上涨速度快于物价，这对工人来说是好消息。

segments.src: It is more complicated if inflation has also been running above the central bank's 2% goal.
segments.tr: 如果通货膨胀率也一直高于央行2%的目标，情况就更复杂了。

segments.src: In that case, solid wage growth can look like a risk to policymakers.
segments.tr: 在这种情况下，稳健的工资增长可能会被决策者视为一种风险。

segments.src: Their concern is that higher labor costs get passed on through prices, especially in service industries where labor is a large share of the bill.
segments.tr: 他们的担忧是，更高的劳动力成本会通过价格转嫁出去，特别是在劳动力成本占账单很大比例的服务行业。

segments.src: Averages also hide differences.
segments.tr: 平均值也掩盖了差异。

segments.src: Workers who change jobs have often received larger raises than those who stay put, while pay increases for people in the same role have been smaller.
segments.tr: 跳槽的员工往往比留任的员工获得了更大的加薪幅度，而担任相同职位的员工薪酬涨幅则较小。

segments.src: Households that carry high rent, mortgage, or credit card costs may still feel stretched even when the national wage figure looks healthy.
segments.tr: 即使全国工资数据看起来很健康，那些承担高额租金、抵押贷款或信用卡费用的家庭可能仍然感到捉襟见肘。

segments.src: ## Job-switching: a sign of confidence, or a fading one
segments.tr: ## 跳槽：信心的标志，还是信心的消退

segments.src: Economists watch how often workers quit voluntarily.
segments.tr: 经济学家会观察员工主动离职的频率。

segments.src: People generally leave a job when they are confident they can find a better one.
segments.tr: 人们通常在确信自己能找到更好的工作时才会离职。

segments.src: A high quit rate suggests a confident labor market with plenty of openings.
segments.tr: 高离职率表明劳动力市场充满信心，且有大量空缺职位。

segments.src: A falling quit rate suggests workers are staying put, and that employers are posting fewer openings.
segments.tr: 下降的离职率表明员工选择留任，且雇主发布的空缺职位减少了。

segments.src: In the past few years, the pace of job-switching has cooled from its peak.
segments.tr: 在过去几年中，跳槽的速度已从峰值回落。

segments.src: That has two effects:
segments.tr: 这产生了两个影响：

segments.src: - **Less pressure on pay.** When fewer people change jobs, employers feel less need to raise wages to compete.
segments.tr: - **薪酬压力减小。** 当跳槽的人减少时，雇主感到提高工资以进行竞争的必要性降低。

segments.src: - **Harder entry for new job seekers.** Fewer vacancies are created when current employees stay in their roles, which can make it tougher for the unemployed and for people entering the workforce.
segments.tr: - **新求职者进入门槛更高。** 当现有员工留在原岗位时，创造的职位空缺就会减少，这可能会使失业者和进入劳动力市场的人更难找到工作。

segments.src: This helps explain why a strong payroll number and a feeling of "a low-hire, low-fire" job market can both be true at once.
segments.tr: 这有助于解释为什么强劲的工资单数据与“低招聘、低解雇”的就业市场感受可以同时成立。

segments.src: ## Why markets read good news as a rate risk
segments.tr: ## 为什么市场将好消息解读为利率风险

segments.src: For many people, the most puzzling part of a jobs report day is that stocks or bonds sometimes fall after good news.
segments.tr: 对许多人来说，就业报告发布日最令人困惑的部分是，股票或债券有时会在好消息发布后下跌。

segments.src: The reason is interest rates.
segments.tr: 原因在于利率。

segments.src: The Federal Reserve sets its policy rate with two goals in mind: maximum employment and stable prices.
segments.tr: 美联储在制定政策利率时考虑两个目标：最大化就业和价格稳定。

segments.src: When the labor market is strong and wages are rising, the case for lowering rates weakens.
segments.tr: 当劳动力市场强劲且工资上涨时，降息的理由就会减弱。

segments.src: Investors who had been counting on rate cuts may have to change their expectations.
segments.tr: 一直指望降息的投资者可能不得不改变他们的预期。

segments.src: Here is how that chain usually works:
segments.tr: 以下是这一链条通常的运作方式：

segments.src: 1. **A stronger-than-expected report** suggests the economy does not need extra support from lower rates.
segments.tr: 1. **好于预期的报告**表明经济不需要通过降息来获得额外支持。

segments.src: 2. **Expectations for rate cuts are pushed back** or reduced.
segments.tr: 2. **降息预期被推迟**或降低。

segments.src: 3. **Government bond yields often rise**, because investors now expect rates to stay higher for longer.
segments.tr: 3. **政府债券收益率往往上升**，因为投资者现在预期利率将在更长时间内保持高位。

segments.src: 4. **Higher yields can weigh on stock prices**, particularly for companies that rely on borrowing or whose value depends heavily on future earnings.
segments.tr: 4. **更高的收益率可能会对股价造成压力**，特别是对于那些依赖借贷或其价值在很大程度上取决于未来收益的公司而言。

segments.src: 5. **Borrowing costs for households stay elevated.** Mortgage rates, auto loans, and credit cards tend to follow broader rate expectations.
segments.tr: 5. **家庭借贷成本保持高位。** 抵押贷款利率、汽车贷款和信用卡利率往往会跟随更广泛的利率预期。

segments.src: This is why a report can be good for workers and still unwelcome for people hoping for cheaper loans.
segments.tr: 这就是为什么一份报告对工人来说可能是好消息，但对希望获得更便宜贷款的人来说却不受欢迎。

segments.src: It also explains why traders often react more to the difference between actual and expected numbers than to the numbers themselves.
segments.tr: 这也解释了为什么交易员对实际数字与预期数字之间的差异的反应，往往比对数字本身的反应更强烈。

segments.src: ## What to watch next
segments.tr: ## 接下来关注什么

segments.src: A single month rarely changes the broader direction.
segments.tr: 单个月份的数据很少会改变大方向。

segments.src: These indicators give a fuller view:
segments.tr: 这些指标提供了更全面的视角：

segments.src: - **Revisions to prior months**, which can change the story of how strong hiring really was.
segments.tr: - **对前几个月的修正**，这可能会改变关于招聘实际强劲程度的叙述。

segments.src: - **Average hourly earnings**, to see whether wage growth is speeding up or slowing down.
segments.tr: - **平均时薪**，以观察工资增长是在加速还是放缓。

segments.src: - **The labor force participation rate**, which shows whether more people are coming back to look for work.
segments.tr: - **劳动力参与率**，这显示是否有更多人重新开始寻找工作。

segments.src: - **Job openings and quit rates**, from the monthly JOLTS survey, for a read on employer demand and worker confidence.
segments.tr: - **职位空缺和离职率**，来自每月的JOLTS调查，用于了解雇主需求和员工信心。

segments.src: - **Weekly jobless claims**, an early signal of layoffs.
segments.tr: - **每周失业救济申请人数**，这是裁员的早期信号。

segments.src: - **Inflation data and Federal Reserve communications**, since these shape how policymakers respond to the labor market.
segments.tr: - **通胀数据和美联储的沟通**，因为这些决定了决策者如何应对劳动力市场。

segments.src: ## The bottom line
segments.tr: ## 总结

segments.src: A report showing 165,000 new jobs and a 4.1% unemployment rate is, by most measures, evidence of a resilient labor market.
segments.tr: 一份显示新增16.5万个就业岗位和4.1%失业率的报告，从大多数指标来看，都是劳动力市场具有韧性的证据。

segments.src: But resilience is not the same as broad-based strength.
segments.tr: 但韧性并不等同于广泛的强劲。

segments.src: Gains concentrated in a few industries, uneven results across age groups, and slower job-switching all suggest that many people are not feeling the benefit equally.
segments.tr: 增长集中在少数几个行业、各年龄组结果不均衡以及跳槽速度放缓，都表明许多人并未平等地感受到这种好处。

segments.src: And because strong employment can delay interest rate cuts, good news for the job market can mean a more cautious outlook for borrowers and investors.
segments.tr: 而且由于强劲的就业可能会推迟降息，对就业市场的好消息可能意味着借款人和投资者将面临更谨慎的前景。

segments.src: The most useful way to read a jobs report is to look past the headline: ask who is being hired, how much they are paid, and what it means for the path of interest rates.
segments.tr: 解读就业报告最有用的方法是透过头条新闻看本质：询问谁被雇用了、他们的薪酬是多少，以及这对利率路径意味着什么。

segments.src: *Figures cited are as reported for October and may be revised.
segments.tr: *所引用的数字为10月份报告的数据，可能会进行修正。

segments.src: Readers should consult official sources, such as the Bureau of Labor Statistics, for the latest data.
segments.tr: 读者应查阅官方来源（如劳工统计局）以获取最新数据。

segments.tr: 本内容仅供参考，不构成财务建议。*

segments.tr: यह लेख बताता है कि आंकड़े क्या सुझाते हैं, अर्थव्यवस्था के लिए मजबूती और परिवारों तथा निवेशकों के लिए राहत हमेशा एक ही बात क्यों नहीं होती है, और आने वाले महीनों में किन विवरणों पर नजर रखना सार्थक है।

segments.src: *This article is for general information only.
segments.tr: *यह लेख केवल सामान्य जानकारी के लिए है।

segments.src: It is not financial, investment, or employment advice.*
segments.tr: यह वित्तीय, निवेश या रोजगार सलाह नहीं है.*

segments.src: ## What the headline numbers say
segments.tr: ## मुख्य आंकड़े क्या कहते हैं

segments.src: The monthly employment report comes from two separate surveys.
segments.tr: मासिक रोजगार रिपोर्ट दो अलग-अलग सर्वेक्षणों से आती है।

segments.src: One asks employers how many people are on their payrolls.
segments.tr: एक नियोक्ताओं से पूछता है कि उनके पेरोल पर कितने लोग हैं।

segments.src: The other asks households whether they are working or looking for work.
segments.tr: दूसरा परिवारों से पूछता है कि क्या वे काम कर रहे हैं या काम की तलाश कर रहे हैं।

segments.src: The 165,000 figure comes from the employer survey.
segments.tr: 165,000 का आंकड़ा नियोक्ता सर्वेक्षण से आता है।

segments.src: The 4.1% unemployment rate comes from the household survey.
segments.tr: 4.1% बेरोजगारी दरhousehold सर्वेक्षण से आती है।

segments.src: A few points of context help:
segments.tr: संदर्भ के कुछ बिंदु मदद करते हैं:

segments.src: - **165,000 is solid, not spectacular.** In a growing economy, a gain in this range is generally enough to absorb new entrants to the labor force. It is not the kind of surge that signals overheating on its own.
segments.tr: - **165,000 ठोस है, शानदार नहीं।** बढ़ती अर्थव्यवस्था में, इस सीमा में वृद्धि आम तौर पर श्रम बल में नए प्रवेशकों को समाहित करने के लिए पर्याप्त होती है। यह उस प्रकार की तेजी नहीं है जो अपने दम पर ओवरहीटिंग का संकेत देती है।

segments.src: - **4.1% is historically low.** By long-run standards, an unemployment rate near 4% is consistent with a tight labor market, where employers compete for workers.
segments.tr: - **4.1% ऐतिहासिक रूप से कम है।** दीर्घकालिक मानकों के अनुसार, 4% के करीब बेरोजगारी दर एक तंग श्रम बाजार के अनुकूल है, जहां नियोक्ता श्रमिकों के लिए प्रतिस्पर्धा करते हैं।

segments.src: - **Beating expectations matters in its own right.** Forecasters publish estimates before each report. A result above the consensus is treated as a surprise, and surprises move markets even when the underlying change is modest.
segments.tr: - **उम्मीदों को पार करना अपने आप में महत्वपूर्ण है।** पूर्वानुमानकर्ता प्रत्येक रिपोर्ट से पहले अनुमान प्रकाशित करते हैं। आम सहमति से ऊपर के परिणाम को आश्चर्य माना जाता है, और जब अंतर्निहित परिवर्तन मामूली हो तब भी आश्चर्य बाजारों को स्थानांतरित करते हैं।

segments.src: - **Numbers get revised.** Initial estimates are often adjusted in later months. One report is a snapshot, not a verdict.
segments.tr: - **संख्याओं में संशोधन किया जाता है।** शुरुआती अनुमानों को अक्सर बाद के महीनों में समायोजित किया जाता है। एक रिपोर्ट एक स्नैपशॉट है, कोई फैसला नहीं।

segments.src: ## Where hiring was strong, and where it wasn't
segments.tr: ## कहां नियुक्तियां मजबूत थीं, और कहां नहीं

segments.src: A headline total can hide very different experiences underneath.
segments.tr: एक मुख्य कुल संख्या नीचे बहुत अलग अनुभवों को छिपा सकती है।

segments.src: In reports like this one, job gains tend to cluster in a small number of sectors, while others stay flat or shrink.
segments.tr: इस तरह की रिपोर्टों में, नौकरी में लाभ कुछ ही क्षेत्रों में केंद्रित होते हैं, जबकि अन्य स्थिर रहते हैं या सिकुड़ते हैं।

segments.src: **Industries.** Health care, social assistance, and government have been consistent sources of job growth in recent years, partly because demand for those services is steady and less sensitive to the business cycle.
segments.tr: **उद्योग।** स्वास्थ्य सेवा, सामाजिक सहायता और सरकार हाल के वर्षों में नौकरी की वृद्धि के लगातार स्रोत रहे हैं, आंशिक रूप से क्योंकि उन सेवाओं की मांग स्थिर है और व्यावसायिक चक्र के प्रति कम संवेदनशील है।

segments.src: Sectors that depend more on discretionary spending or interest rates, such as parts of manufacturing, construction, retail, and information technology, have tended to be more volatile.
segments.tr: वे क्षेत्र जो विवेकाधीन खर्च या ब्याज दरों पर अधिक निर्भर करते हैं, जैसे कि विनिर्माण, निर्माण, खुदरा और सूचना प्रौद्योगिकी के कुछ हिस्से, अधिक अस्थिर रहे हैं।

segments.src: When most of the gains come from a few areas, a strong total can coexist with real weakness elsewhere.
segments.tr: जब अधिकांश लाभ कुछ क्षेत्रों से आते हैं, तो एक मजबूत कुल संख्या अन्य जगहों पर वास्तविक कमजोरी के साथ सह-अस्तित्व में हो सकती है।

segments.src: **Age groups.** Workers in their prime working years, roughly 25 to 54, have had very high employment rates.
segments.tr: **आयु वर्ग।** अपने प्रमुख कामकाजी वर्षों में श्रमिक, लगभग 25 से 54 वर्ष, की रोजगार दर बहुत अधिक रही है।

segments.src: Younger workers and new graduates often face a harder search when employers slow hiring for entry-level roles.
segments.tr: युवा श्रमिकों और नए स्नातकों को अक्सर कठिन खोज का सामना करना पड़ता है जब नियोक्ता प्रवेश स्तर की भूमिकाओं के लिए नियुक्ति धीमी कर देते हैं।

segments.src: Older workers who lose a job may take longer to find a new one.
segments.tr: **older** श्रमिकों को नौकरी खोने पर नया खोजने में अधिक समय लग सकता है।

segments.src: The overall unemployment rate averages all of this out, which is why a good headline can feel out of step with what some job seekers report.
segments.tr: समग्र बेरोजगारी दर इन सबका औसत निकालती है, यही वजह है कि एक अच्छी हेडलाइन कुछ नौकरी चाहने वालों की रिपोर्ट के साथ तालमेल से बाहर महसूस हो सकती है।

segments.src: **Hours and job quality.** The count of jobs does not show whether positions are full-time, part-time, or temporary.
segments.tr: **घंटे और नौकरी की गुणवत्ता।** नौकरियों की गिनती यह नहीं दिखाती है कि पद पूर्णकालिक, अंशकालिक या अस्थायी हैं।

segments.src: Analysts also look at average weekly hours and at the share of people working part-time who would prefer full-time work.
segments.tr: विश्लेषक औसत साप्ताहिक घंटों और अंशकालिक काम करने वाले लोगों के उस हिस्से को भी देखते हैं जो पूर्णकालिक काम पसंद करते।

segments.src: ## Wages: growing, but is it enough?
segments.tr: **वेतन: बढ़ रहा है, लेकिन क्या यह पर्याप्त है?**

segments.src: Pay is the second half of the story.
segments.tr: वेतन कहानी का दूसरा आधा हिस्सा है।

segments.src: When unemployment is low, employers usually have to offer more to attract and keep workers, so wage growth tends to stay firm.
segments.tr: जब बेरोजगारी कम होती है, तो नियोक्ताओं को आम तौर पर श्रमिकों को आकर्षित करने और बनाए रखने के लिए अधिक पेशकश करनी पड़ती है, इसलिए वेतन वृद्धि मजबूत बनी रहती है।

segments.src: That is good news for workers if pay rises faster than prices.
segments.tr: यदि वेतन कीमतों की तुलना में तेजी से बढ़ता है तो यह श्रमिकों के लिए अच्छी खबर है।

segments.src: It is more complicated if inflation has also been running above the central bank's 2% goal.
segments.tr: यह अधिक जटिल है यदि मुद्रास्फीति भी केंद्रीय बैंक के 2% लक्ष्य से ऊपर चल रही है।

segments.src: In that case, solid wage growth can look like a risk to policymakers.
segments.tr: उस स्थिति में, ठोस वेतन वृद्धि नीति निर्माताओं के लिए जोखिम की तरह दिख सकती है।

segments.src: Their concern is that higher labor costs get passed on through prices, especially in service industries where labor is a large share of the bill.
segments.tr: उनकी चिंता यह है कि उच्च श्रम लागत कीमतों के माध्यम से पारित हो जाती है, विशेष रूप से सेवा उद्योगों में जहां श्रम बिल का एक बड़ा हिस्सा है।

segments.src: Averages also hide differences.
segments.tr: औसत अंतर भी छिपाते हैं।

segments.src: Workers who change jobs have often received larger raises than those who stay put, while pay increases for people in the same role have been smaller.
segments.tr: नौकरी बदलने वाले श्रमिकों को अक्सर उन लोगों की तुलना में बड़ी वृद्धि मिली है जो अपनी जगह पर बने रहे, जबकि एक ही भूमिका में लोगों के लिए वेतन वृद्धि छोटी रही है।

segments.src: Households that carry high rent, mortgage, or credit card costs may still feel stretched even when the national wage figure looks healthy.
segments.tr: उच्च किराए, बंधक या क्रेडिट कार्ड लागत का वहन करने वाले परिवार राष्ट्रीय वेतन का आंकड़ा स्वस्थ दिखने पर भी तनाव महसूस कर सकते हैं।

segments.src: ## Job-switching: a sign of confidence, or a fading one
segments.tr: ## नौकरी-बदलना: आत्मविश्वास का संकेत, या फीका पड़ता हुआ संकेत

segments.src: Economists watch how often workers quit voluntarily.
segments.tr: अर्थशास्त्री इस बात पर नजर रखते हैं कि कितनी बार श्रमिक स्वेच्छा से नौकरी छोड़ते हैं।

segments.src: People generally leave a job when they are confident they can find a better one.
segments.tr: लोग आम तौर पर नौकरी तब छोड़ते हैं जब उन्हें विश्वास होता है कि वे बेहतर नौकरी पा सकते हैं।

segments.src: A high quit rate suggests a confident labor market with plenty of openings.
segments.tr: उच्च छोड़ने की दर पर्याप्त रिक्तियों के साथ एक आश्वस्त श्रम बाजार का सुझाव देती है।

segments.src: A falling quit rate suggests workers are staying put, and that employers are posting fewer openings.
segments.tr: घटती छोड़ने की दर बताती है कि श्रमिक अपनी जगह पर बने हुए हैं, और नियोक्ता कम रिक्तियां पोस्ट कर रहे हैं।

segments.src: In the past few years, the pace of job-switching has cooled from its peak.
segments.tr: पिछले कुछ वर्षों में, नौकरी बदलने की गति अपने चरम से ठंडी हो गई है।

segments.src: That has two effects:
segments.tr: इसके दो प्रभाव हैं:

segments.src: - **Less pressure on pay.** When fewer people change jobs, employers feel less need to raise wages to compete.
segments.tr: - **वेतन पर कम दबाव।** जब कम लोग नौकरियां बदलते हैं, तो नियोक्ताओं को प्रतिस्पर्धा करने के लिए वेतन बढ़ाने की कम आवश्यकता महसूस होती है।

segments.src: - **Harder entry for new job seekers.** Fewer vacancies are created when current employees stay in their roles, which can make it tougher for the unemployed and for people entering the workforce.
segments.tr: - **नए नौकरी चाहने वालों के लिए कठिन प्रवेश।** जब वर्तमान कर्मचारी अपनी भूमिकाओं में बने रहते हैं तो कम रिक्तियां बनती हैं, जिससे बेरोजगारों और कार्यबल में प्रवेश करने वाले लोगों के लिए यह कठिन हो सकता है।

segments.src: This helps explain why a strong payroll number and a feeling of "a low-hire, low-fire" job market can both be true at once.
segments.tr: यह समझाने में मदद करता है कि एक मजबूत पेरोल संख्या और "कम-नियुक्ति, कम-निकालने" के श्रम बाजार की भावना दोनों एक साथ कैसे सच हो सकती हैं।

segments.src: ## Why markets read good news as a rate risk
segments.tr: ## बाजार अच्छी खबर को दर जोखिम के रूप में क्यों पढ़ते हैं

segments.src: For many people, the most puzzling part of a jobs report day is that stocks or bonds sometimes fall after good news.
segments.tr: कई लोगों के लिए, नौकरी रिपोर्ट के दिन का सबसे भ्रमित करने वाला हिस्सा यह है कि अच्छी खबर के बाद स्टॉक या बॉन्ड कभी-कभी गिर जाते हैं।

segments.src: The reason is interest rates.
segments.tr: इसका कारण ब्याज दरें हैं।

segments.src: The Federal Reserve sets its policy rate with two goals in mind: maximum employment and stable prices.
segments.tr: फेडरल रिजर्व दो लक्ष्यों को ध्यान में रखकर अपनी नीतिगत दर तय करता है: अधिकतम रोजगार और स्थिर कीमतें।

segments.src: When the labor market is strong and wages are rising, the case for lowering rates weakens.
segments.tr: जब श्रम बाजार मजबूत होता है और वेतन बढ़ रहा होता है, तो दरों को कम करने का मामला कमजोर हो जाता है।

segments.src: Investors who had been counting on rate cuts may have to change their expectations.
segments.tr: जो निवेशक दर में कटौती पर भरोसा कर रहे थे, उन्हें अपनी उम्मीदें बदलनी पड़ सकती हैं।

segments.src: Here is how that chain usually works:
segments.tr: यहाँ बताया गया है कि वह श्रृंखला आमतौर पर कैसे काम करती है:

segments.src: 1. **A stronger-than-expected report** suggests the economy does not need extra support from lower rates.
segments.tr: 1. **एक उम्मीद से अधिक मजबूत रिपोर्ट** बताती है कि अर्थव्यवस्था को कम दरों से अतिरिक्त समर्थन की आवश्यकता नहीं है।

segments.src: 2. **Expectations for rate cuts are pushed back** or reduced.
segments.tr: 2. **दर में कटौती की उम्मीदों को पीछे धकेल दिया जाता है** या कम कर दिया जाता है।

segments.src: 3. **Government bond yields often rise**, because investors now expect rates to stay higher for longer.
segments.tr: 3. **सरकारी बॉन्ड यील्ड अक्सर बढ़ जाती है**, क्योंकि निवेशकों को अब उम्मीद है कि दरें लंबे समय तक ऊंची रहेंगी।

segments.src: 4. **Higher yields can weigh on stock prices**, particularly for companies that rely on borrowing or whose value depends heavily on future earnings.
segments.tr: 4. **उच्च यील्ड स्टॉक की कीमतों पर वजन डाल सकती है**, विशेष रूप से उन कंपनियों के लिए जो उधार लेने पर निर्भर करती हैं या जिनका मूल्य भविष्य की कमाई पर बहुत अधिक निर्भर करता है।

segments.src: 5. **Borrowing costs for households stay elevated.** Mortgage rates, auto loans, and credit cards tend to follow broader rate expectations.
segments.tr: 5. **घरों के लिए उधार लेने की लागत ऊंची बनी रहती है।** बंधक दरें, ऑटो ऋण और क्रेडिट कार्ड व्यापक दर अपेक्षाओं का पालन करते हैं।

segments.src: This is why a report can be good for workers and still unwelcome for people hoping for cheaper loans.
segments.tr: यही कारण है कि एक रिपोर्ट श्रमिकों के लिए अच्छी हो सकती है और फिर भी सस्ते ऋण की उम्मीद करने वाले लोगों के लिए अवांछित हो सकती है।

segments.src: It also explains why traders often react more to the difference between actual and expected numbers than to the numbers themselves.

segments.tr: - **165,000 رقم قوي، لكنه ليس مذهلاً.** في اقتصاد نامٍ، تعود زيادة في هذا النطاق بشكل عام بالنفع الكافي لاستيعاب الوافدين الجدد إلى القوى العاملة. وهي ليست من نوع الطفرة التي تشير بمفردها إلى التضخم المفرط.

segments.src: - **4.1% is historically low.** By long-run standards, an unemployment rate near 4% is consistent with a tight labor market, where employers compete for workers.
segments.tr: - **4.1% رقم منخفض تاريخيًا.** بالمعايير طويلة الأجل، يتوافق معدل بطالة قريب من 4% مع سوق عمل مشدود، حيث يتنافس أصحاب العمل على العمال.

segments.src: - **Beating expectations matters in its own right.** Forecasters publish estimates before each report. A result above the consensus is treated as a surprise, and surprises move markets even when the underlying change is modest.
segments.tr: - **تفوق التوقعات له أهمية خاصة.** ينشر المحللون تقديرات قبل كل تقرير. وتُعامل النتيجة التي تتجاوز الإجماع على أنها مفاجأة، والمفاجآت تحرك الأسواق حتى لو كان التغيير الأساسي متواضعًا.

segments.src: - **Numbers get revised.** Initial estimates are often adjusted in later months. One report is a snapshot, not a verdict.
segments.tr: - **تخضع الأرقام للمراجعة.** غالبًا ما تُعدل التقديرات الأولية في أشهر لاحقة. فالتقرير الواحد هو لقطة سريعة وليس حكمًا نهائيًا.

segments.src: ## Where hiring was strong, and where it wasn't
segments.tr: ## أين كان التوظيف قويًا، وأين لم يكن؟

segments.src: A headline total can hide very different experiences underneath.
segments.tr: يمكن للإجمالي الرئيسي أن يخفي تجارب مختلفة تمامًا تحته.

segments.src: In reports like this one, job gains tend to cluster in a small number of sectors, while others stay flat or shrink.
segments.tr: في تقارير مثل هذا التقرير، تميل مكاسب الوظائف إلى التجمع في عدد صغير من القطاعات، بينما تظل قطاعات أخرى ركودية أو تنكمش.

segments.src: **Industries.** Health care, social assistance, and government have been consistent sources of job growth in recent years, partly because demand for those services is steady and less sensitive to the business cycle.
segments.tr: **القطاعات.** كانت الرعاية الصحية، والمساعدة الاجتماعية، والحكومة مصادر مستمرة لنمو الوظائف في السنوات الأخيرة، ويرجع ذلك جزئيًا إلى أن الطلب على هذه الخدمات مستقر وأقل حساسية للدورة الاقتصادية.

segments.src: Sectors that depend more on discretionary spending or interest rates, such as parts of manufacturing, construction, retail, and information technology, have tended to be more volatile.
segments.tr: أما القطاعات التي تعتمد أكثر على الإنفاق الاختياري أو أسعار الفائدة، مثل بعض أجزاء التصنيع، والبناء، والتجزئة، وتكنولوجيا المعلومات، فقد مالت إلى أن تكون أكثر تقلبًا.

segments.src: When most of the gains come from a few areas, a strong total can coexist with real weakness elsewhere.
segments.tr: عندما تأتي معظم المكاسب من مجالات قليلة، يمكن لإجمالي قوي أن يتعايش مع ضعف حقيقي في أماكن أخرى.

segments.src: **Age groups.** Workers in their prime working years, roughly 25 to 54, have had very high employment rates.
segments.tr: **الفئات العمرية.** حقق العمال في سنوات ذروة عطائهم المهني، من 25 إلى 54 عامًا تقريبًا، معدلات توظيف مرتفعة جدًا.

segments.src: Younger workers and new graduates often face a harder search when employers slow hiring for entry-level roles.
segments.tr: غالبًا ما يواجه العمال الأصغر سنًا والخريجون الجدد صعوبة أكبر في البحث عندما يبطئ أصحاب العمل التوظيف في الأدوار المبتدئة.

segments.src: Older workers who lose a job may take longer to find a new one.
segments.tr: وقد يستغرق العمال الكبار الذين يفقدون وظائفهم وقتًا أطول للعثور على وظيفة جديدة.

segments.src: The overall unemployment rate averages all of this out, which is why a good headline can feel out of step with what some job seekers report.
segments.tr: يأخذ معدل البطالة الإجمالي متوسط كل هذا، ولهذا السبب يمكن أن يبدو الرقم الرئيسي الجيد غير متوافق مع ما يواجهه بعض الباحثين عن عمل.

segments.src: **Hours and job quality.** The count of jobs does not show whether positions are full-time, part-time, or temporary.
segments.tr: **ساعات العمل وجودة الوظيفة.** لا يوضح عدد الوظائف ما إذا كانت الوظائف بدوام كامل، أم بدوام جزئي، أم مؤقتة.

segments.src: Analysts also look at average weekly hours and at the share of people working part-time who would prefer full-time work.
segments.tr: ينظر المحللون أيضًا إلى متوسط ساعات العمل الأسبوعية ونسبة الأشخاص الذين يعملون بدوام جزئي ويفضلون العمل بدوام كامل.

segments.src: ## Wages: growing, but is it enough?
segments.tr: ## الأجور: تنمو، ولكن هل هذا كافٍ؟

segments.src: Pay is the second half of the story.
segments.tr: الأجور هي النصف الثاني من القصة.

segments.src: When unemployment is low, employers usually have to offer more to attract and keep workers, so wage growth tends to stay firm.
segments.tr: عندما تكون البطالة منخفضة، يتعين على أصحاب العمل عادةً تقديم المزيد لجذب العمال والاحتفاظ بهم، لذلك يميل نمو الأجور إلى البقاء قويًا.

segments.src: That is good news for workers if pay rises faster than prices.
segments.tr: وهذا خبر سار للعمال إذا ارتفعت الأجور بمعدل أسرع من الأسعار.

segments.src: It is more complicated if inflation has also been running above the central bank's 2% goal.
segments.tr: لكن الأمر يتطلب مزيدًا من التعقيد إذا كان التضخم يسير أيضًا أعلى من هدف البنك المركزي البالغ 2%.

segments.src: In that case, solid wage growth can look like a risk to policymakers.
segments.tr: في هذه الحالة، يمكن أن يبدو نمو الأجور القوي خطرًا بالنسبة لصانعي السياسات.

segments.src: Their concern is that higher labor costs get passed on through prices, especially in service industries where labor is a large share of the bill.
segments.tr: ويكمن قلقهم في أن تكاليف العمالة المرتفعة تُمَرَّر عبر الأسعار، خاصة في قطاعات الخدمات حيث تشكل العمالة حصة كبيرة من الفاتورة.

segments.src: Averages also hide differences.
segments.tr: المتوسطات تخفي الاختلافات أيضًا.

segments.src: Workers who change jobs have often received larger raises than those who stay put, while pay increases for people in the same role have been smaller.
segments.tr: العمال الذين يغيرون وظائفهم غالبًا ما يحصلون على زيادات أكبر من أولئك الذين يبقون في أماكنهم، بينما كانت زيادات الأجور للأشخاص في نفس الدور أصغر.

segments.src: Households that carry high rent, mortgage, or credit card costs may still feel stretched even when the national wage figure looks healthy.
segments.tr: الأسر التي تتحمل تكاليف إيجار أو رهون عقارية أو بطاقات ائتمان مرتفعة قد تظل تشعر بالضغط حتى عندما يبدو رقم الأجور الوطني صحيًا.

segments.src: ## Job-switching: a sign of confidence, or a fading one
segments.tr: ## تغيير الوظائف: علامة على الثقة، أم علامة متلاشية؟

segments.src: Economists watch how often workers quit voluntarily.
segments.tr: يراقب الاقتصادكون كم مرة يترك العمال وظائفهم طواعية.

segments.src: People generally leave a job when they are confident they can find a better one.
segments.tr: يترك الناس الوظيفة عمومًا عندما يكونون واثقين من قدرتهم على العثور على وظيفة أفضل.

segments.src: A high quit rate suggests a confident labor market with plenty of openings.
segments.tr: يشير معدل الاستقالة المرتفع إلى سوق عمل واثق به الكثير من الفرص المتاحة.

segments.src: A falling quit rate suggests workers are staying put, and that employers are posting fewer openings.
segments.tr: بينما يشير انخفاض معدل الاستقالة إلى أن العمال يفضلون البقاء في أماكنهم، وأن أصحاب العمل يعلنون عن فرص أقل.

segments.src: In the past few years, the pace of job-switching has cooled from its peak.
segments.tr: في السنوات القليلة الماضية، تباطأ معدل تغيير الوظائف عن ذروته.

segments.src: That has two effects:
segments.tr: ولهذا نتيجتان:

segments.src: - **Less pressure on pay.** When fewer people change jobs, employers feel less need to raise wages to compete.
segments.tr: - **ضغط أقل على الأجور.** عندما يغير عدد أقل من الناس وظائفهم، يشعر أصحاب العمل بحاجة أقل لرفع الأجور للمنافسة.

segments.src: - **Harder entry for new job seekers.** Fewer vacancies are created when current employees stay in their roles, which can make it tougher for the unemployed and for people entering the workforce.
segments.tr: - **صعوبة أكبر للباحثين الجدد عن عمل.** يتم إنشاء عدد أقل من الشواغر عندما يظل الموظفون الحاليون في أدوارهم، مما قد يجعل الأمر أكثر صعوبة على العاطلين عن العمل وعلى الأشخاص الذين يدخلون القوى العاملة حديثًا.

segments.src: This helps explain why a strong payroll number and a feeling of "a low-hire, low-fire" job market can both be true at once.
segments.tr: يساعد هذا في شرح لماذا يمكن لرقم كشوف المرتبات القوي والشعور بسوق عمل "منخفض التوظيف ومنخفض التسريح" أن يكونا صحيحين في وقت واحد.

segments.src: ## Why markets read good news as a rate risk
segments.tr: ## لماذا تقرأ الأسواق الأخبار الجيدة على أنها خطر على أسعار الفائدة؟

segments.src: For many people, the most puzzling part of a jobs report day is that stocks or bonds sometimes fall after good news.
segments.tr: بالنسبة للعديد من الناس، فإن الجزء الأكثر إرباكًا في يوم صدور تقرير الوظائف هو أن الأسهم أو السندات تنخفض أحيانًا بعد الأخبار الجيدة.

segments.src: The reason is interest rates.
segments.tr: والسبب هو أسعار الفائدة.

segments.src: The Federal Reserve sets its policy rate with two goals in mind: maximum employment and stable prices.
segments.tr: يحدد الاحتياطي الفيدرالي سعر سياسته بهدفين في الاعتبار: التوظيف الكامل واستقرار الأسعار.

segments.src: When the labor market is strong and wages are rising, the case for lowering rates weakens.
segments.tr: عندما تكون سوق العمل قوية والأجور ترتفع، تضعف حجة خفض الفائدة.

segments.src: Investors who had been counting on rate cuts may have to change their expectations.
segments.tr: المستثمرون الذين كانوا يعتمدون على خفض أسعار الفائدة قد يضطرون إلى تغيير توقعاتهم.

segments.src: Here is how that chain usually works:
segments.tr: إليك كيف تعمل تلك السلسلة عادةً:

segments.src: 1. **A stronger-than-expected report** suggests the economy does not need extra support from lower rates.
segments.tr: 1. **تقرير أقوى من المتوقع** يشير إلى أن الاقتصاد لا يحتاج إلى دعم إضافي من خفض أسعار الفائدة.

segments.src: 2. **Expectations for rate cuts are pushed back** or reduced.
segments.tr: 2. **يتم تأجيل التوقعات بخفض أسعار الفائدة** أو تقليصها.

segments.src: 3. **Government bond yields often rise**, because investors now expect rates to stay higher for longer.
segments.tr: 3. **عائدات السندات الحكومية ترتفع غالباً**، لأن المستثمرين يتوقعون الآن بقاء أسعار الفائدة أعلى لفترة أطول.

segments.src: 4. **Higher yields can weigh on stock prices**, particularly for companies that rely on borrowing or whose value depends heavily on future earnings.
segments.tr: 4. **يمكن للعائدات المرتفعة أن تضغط على أسعار الأسهم**، خاصة للشركات التي تعتمد على الاقتراض أو التي تعتمد قيمتها بشكل كبير على الأرباح المستقبلية.

segments.src: 5. **Borrowing costs for households stay elevated.** Mortgage rates, auto loans, and credit cards tend to follow broader rate expectations.
segments.tr: 5. **تبقى تكاليف الاقتراض للأسر مرتفعة.** تميل معدلات الرهن العقاري، وقروض السيارات، وبطاقات الائتمان إلى اتباع توقعات أسعار الفائدة الأوسع.

segments.src: This is why a report can be good for workers and still unwelcome for people hoping for cheaper loans.
segments.tr: لهذا السبب يمكن لتقرير أن يكون جيدًا للعمال ولكنه غير مرحب به للأشخاص الذين يأملون في قروض أرخص.

segments.src: It also explains why traders often react more to the difference between actual and expected numbers than to the numbers themselves.
segments.tr: ويشرح هذا أيضًا لماذا يتفاعل المتداولون غالبًا مع الفرق بين الأرقام الفعلية والمتوقعة أكثر من تفاعلهم مع الأرقام نفسها.

segments.src: ## What to watch next
segments.tr: ## ما يجب مراقبته بعد ذلك

segments.src: A single month rarely changes the broader direction.
segments.tr: نادرًا ما يغير شهر واحد الاتجاه الأوسع.

segments.src: These indicators give a fuller view:
segments.tr: تعطي هذه المؤشرات نظرة أكثر اكتمالاً:

segments.src: - **Revisions to prior months**, which can change the story of how strong hiring really was.
segments.tr: - **المراجعات للأشهر السابقة**، والتي يمكن أن تغير قصة مدى قوة التوظيف حقًا.

segments.src: - **Average hourly earnings**, to see whether wage growth is speeding up or slowing down.
segments.tr: - **متوسط الكسب في الساعة**، لمعرفة ما إذا كان نمو الأجور يتسارع أم يتباطأ.

segments.src: - **The labor force participation rate**, which shows whether more people are coming back to look for work.
segments.tr: - **معدل المشاركة في القوى العاملة**، الذي يوضح ما إذا كان المزيد من الناس يعودون للبحث عن عمل.

segments.src: - **Job openings and quit rates**, from the monthly JOLTS survey, for a read on employer demand and worker confidence.
segments.tr: - **فرص العمل ومعدلات الاستقالة**، من مسح JOLTS الشهري، لقراءة طلب أصحاب العمل وثقة العمال.

segments.src: - **Weekly jobless claims**, an early signal of layoffs.
segments.tr: - **طلبات إعانة البطالة الأسبوعية**، كإشارة مبكرة على تسريح العمال.

segments.src: - **Inflation data and Federal Reserve communications**, since these shape how policymakers respond to the labor market.
segments.tr: - **بيانات التضخم وتصريحات الاحتياطي الفيدرالي**، لأنها تشكل كيفية استجابة صانعي السياسات لسوق العمل.

segments.src: ## The bottom line
segments.tr: ## الخلاصة

segments.src: A report showing 165,000 new jobs and a 4.1% unemployment rate is, by most measures, evidence of a resilient labor market.
segments.tr: إن تقريرًا يُظهر 165,000 وظيفة جديدة ومعدل بطالة يبلغ 4.1% هو، بمعظم المعايير، دليل على سوق عمل مرن.

segments.src: But resilience is not the same as broad-based strength.
segments.tr: لكن المرونة ليست هي نفسها القوة الواسعة النطاق.

segments.src: Gains concentrated in a few industries, uneven results across age groups, and slower job-switching all suggest that many people are not feeling the benefit equally.
segments.tr: المكاسب المتركزة في قطاعات قليلة، والنتائج غير المتكافئة عبر الفئات العمرية، وتباطؤ تغيير الوظائف تظهر كلها أن العديد من الناس لا يشعرون بالفائدة بشكل متساوٍ.

segments.src: And because strong employment can delay interest rate cuts, good news for the job market can mean a more cautious outlook for borrowers and investors.
segments.tr: ولأن التوظيف القوي يمكن أن يؤخر خفض أسعار الفائدة، فإن الأخبار الجيدة لسوق العمل قد تعني آفاقًا أكثر حذرًا للمقترضين والمستثمرين.

segments.src: The most useful way to read a jobs report is to look past the headline: ask who is being hired, how much they are paid, and what it means for the path of interest rates.
segments.tr: الطريقة الأكثر فائدة لقراءة تقرير الوظائف هي النظر إلى ما وراء الرقم الرئيسي: اسأل من الذي يتم توظيفه، وكم يُدفع لهم، وما الذي يعنيه ذلك لمسار أسعار الفائدة.

segments.src: *Figures cited are as reported for October and may be revised.
segments.tr: *الأرقام المذكورة هي كما تم الإبلاغ عنها لشهر أكتوبر وقد تخضع للمراجعة.

segments.src: Readers should consult official sources, such as the Bureau of Labor Statistics, for the latest data.
segments.tr: يجب على القراء مراجعة المصادر الرسمية، مثل مكتب إحصاءات العمل، للحصول على أحدث البيانات.

fr.title: 165 000 emplois et 4,1 % de chômage : pourquoi un bon rapport d'octobre n'est pas une bonne nouvelle pour tout le monde

segments.src: A monthly jobs report is often summed up in a single headline number.
segments.tr: Un rapport mensuel sur l'emploi est souvent résumé par un seul chiffre principal.

segments.src: For October, that number was 165,000 jobs added, with the unemployment rate at 4.1%.
segments.tr: Pour octobre, ce chiffre était de 165 000 emplois créés, avec un taux de chômage à 4,1 %.

segments.src: Payrolls came in above what forecasters expected, and on the surface that looks like good news.
segments.tr: Les créations d'emplois ont dépassé les prévisions, ce qui, en apparence, ressemble à une bonne nouvelle.

segments.src: Look closer and the picture is more mixed.
segments.tr: Regardez de plus près et le tableau est plus nuancé.

segments.src: Hiring was uneven across industries and age groups, and financial markets tend to treat a strong labor market as a reason to expect higher borrowing costs for longer.
segments.tr: L'embauche a été inégale selon les secteurs et les groupes d'âge, et les marchés financiers ont tendance à considérer un marché du travail solide comme une raison d'anticiper des coûts d'emprunt plus élevés plus longtemps.

segments.src: This article walks through what the figures suggest, why strength for the economy and relief for households and investors are not always the same thing, and which details are worth watching in the months ahead.
segments.tr: Cet article analyse ce que suggèrent ces chiffres, pourquoi la vigueur de l'économie et le soulagement des ménages et des investisseurs ne vont pas toujours de pair, et quels détails il convient de surveiller dans les mois à venir.

segments.src: *This article is for general information only.
segments.tr: *Cet article est fourni à des fins d'information générale uniquement.

segments.src: It is not financial, investment, or employment advice.*
segments.tr: Il ne constitue pas un conseil financier, en matière d'investissement ou d'emploi.*

segments.src: ## What the headline numbers say
segments.tr: ## What the headline numbers say

segments.src: The monthly employment report comes from two separate surveys.
segments.tr: Le rapport mensuel sur l'emploi provient de deux enquêtes distinctes.

segments.src: One asks employers how many people are on their payrolls.
segments.tr: L'une demande aux employeurs combien de personnes figurent sur leur liste de paie.

segments.src: The other asks households whether they are working or looking for work.
segments.tr: L'autre demande aux ménages s'ils travaillent ou recherchent un emploi.

segments.src: The 165,000 figure comes from the employer survey.
segments.tr: Le chiffre de 165 000 provient de l'enquête auprès des employeurs.

segments.src: The 4.1% unemployment rate comes from the household survey.
segments.tr: Le taux de chômage de 4,1 % provient de l'enquête auprès des ménages.

segments.src: A few points of context help:
segments.tr: Quelques points de contexte sont utiles :

segments.src: - **165,000 is solid, not spectacular.** In a growing economy, a gain in this range is generally enough to absorb new entrants to the labor force. It is not the kind of surge that signals overheating on its own.
segments.tr: - **165 000 is solid, not spectacular.** Dans une économie en croissance, une hausse de cette ampleur suffit généralement à absorber les nouveaux entrants sur le marché du travail. Ce n'est pas le genre de flambée qui signale une surchauffe à elle seule.

segments.src: - **4.1% is historically low.** By long-run standards, an unemployment rate near 4% is consistent with a tight labor market, where employers compete for workers.
segments.tr: - **4,1% is historically low.** Selon les normes à long terme, un taux de chômage proche de 4 % est cohérent avec un marché du travail tendu, où les employeurs se disputent les travailleurs.

segments.src: - **Beating expectations matters in its own right.** Forecasters publish estimates before each report. A result above the consensus is treated as a surprise, and surprises move markets even when the underlying change is modest.
segments.tr: - **Beating expectations matters in its own right.** Les prévisionnistes publient des estimations avant chaque rapport. Un résultat supérieur au consensus est considéré comme une surprise, et les surprises font bouger les marchés même lorsque sous-jacent le changement est modeste.

segments.src: - **Numbers get revised.** Initial estimates are often adjusted in later months. One report is a snapshot, not a verdict.
segments.tr: - **Numbers get revised.** Les estimations initiales sont souvent ajustées les mois suivants. Un rapport est un instantané, pas un verdict.

segments.src: ## Where hiring was strong, and where it wasn't
segments.tr: ## Where hiring was strong, and where it wasn't

segments.src: A headline total can hide very different experiences underneath.
segments.tr: Un total principal peut masquer des réalités très différentes en dessous.

segments.src: In reports like this one, job gains tend to cluster in a small number of sectors, while others stay flat or shrink.
segments.tr: Dans des rapports comme celui-ci, les créations d'emplois ont tendance à se concentrer dans un petit nombre de secteurs, tandis que d'autres stagnent ou se contractent.

segments.src: **Industries.** Health care, social assistance, and government have been consistent sources of job growth in recent years, partly because demand for those services is steady and less sensitive to the business cycle.
segments.tr: **Industries.** La santé, l'aide sociale et les services publics ont été des sources régulières de croissance de l'emploi ces dernières années, en partie parce que la demande pour ces services est stable et moins sensible au cycle économique.

segments.src: Sectors that depend more on discretionary spending or interest rates, such as parts of manufacturing, construction, retail, and information technology, have tended to be more volatile.
segments.tr: Les secteurs qui dépendent davantage des dépenses discrétionnaires ou des taux d'intérêt, tels que certaines parties de l'industrie manufacturière, de la construction, du commerce de détail et des technologies de l'information, ont eu tendance à être plus volatils.

segments.src: When most of the gains come from a few areas, a strong total can coexist with real weakness elsewhere.
segments.tr: Lorsque la majorité des gains proviennent de quelques domaines, un total solide peut coexister avec une réelle faiblesse ailleurs.

segments.src: **Age groups.** Workers in their prime working years, roughly 25 to 54, have had very high employment rates.
segments.tr: **Age groups.** Les travailleurs dans leurs années d'activité principales, soit approximativement de 25 à 54 ans, ont connu des taux d'emploi très élevés.

segments.src: Younger workers and new graduates often face a harder search when employers slow hiring for entry-level roles.
segments.tr: Les jeunes travailleurs et les nouveaux diplômés font souvent face à une recherche plus difficile lorsque les employeurs ralentissent les embauches pour les postes de débutants.

segments.src: Older workers who lose a job may take longer to find a new one.
segments.tr: Les travailleurs plus âgés qui perdent leur emploi peuvent mettre plus de temps à en retrouver un nouveau.

segments.src: The overall unemployment rate averages all of this out, which is why a good headline can feel out of step with what some job seekers report.
segments.tr: Le taux de chômage global fait la moyenne de tout cela, ce qui explique pourquoi un bon chiffre principal peut sembler en décalage avec ce que rapportent certains demandeurs d'emploi.

segments.src: **Hours and job quality.** The count of jobs does not show whether positions are full-time, part-time, or temporary.
segments.tr: **Hours and job quality.** Le décompte des emplois n'indique pas si les postes sont à temps plein, à temps partiel ou temporaires.

segments.src: Analysts also look at average weekly hours and at the share of people working part-time who would prefer full-time work.
segments.tr: Les analystes examinent également le nombre moyen d'heures hebdomadaires et la proportion de personnes travaillant à temps partiel qui préféreraient un emploi à temps plein.

segments.src: ## Wages: growing, but is it enough?
segments.tr: ## Wages: growing, but is it enough?

segments.src: Pay is the second half of the story.
segments.tr: La rémunération est la seconde moitié de l'histoire.

segments.src: When unemployment is low, employers usually have to offer more to attract and keep workers, so wage growth tends to stay firm.
segments.tr: Lorsque le chômage est bas, les employeurs doivent généralement offrir davantage pour attirer et retenir les travailleurs, de sorte que la croissance des salaires a tendance à rester ferme.

segments.src: That is good news for workers if pay rises faster than prices.
segments.tr: C'est une bonne nouvelle pour les travailleurs si la rémunération augmente plus vite que les prix.

segments.src: It is more complicated if inflation has also been running above the central bank's 2% goal.
segments.tr: C'est plus compliqué si l'inflation est également restée supérieure à l'objectif de 2 % de la banque centrale.

segments.src: In that case, solid wage growth can look like a risk to policymakers.
segments.tr: Dans ce cas, une solide croissance des salaires peut apparaître comme un risque pour les décideurs politiques.

segments.src: Their concern is that higher labor costs get passed on through prices, especially in service industries where labor is a large share of the bill.
segments.tr: Leur préoccupation est que des coûts de main-d'œuvre plus élevés se répercutent sur les prix, en particulier dans les industries de services où la main-d'œuvre représente une part importante de la facture.

segments.src: Averages also hide differences.
segments.tr: Les moyennes masquent également les différences.

segments.src: Workers who change jobs have often received larger raises than those who stay put, while pay increases for people in the same role have been smaller.
segments.tr: Les travailleurs qui changent d'emploi ont souvent reçu des augmentations plus importantes que ceux qui restent en place, tandis que les hausses de salaire pour les personnes occupant le même poste ont été plus modestes.

segments.src: Households that carry high rent, mortgage, or credit card costs may still feel stretched even when the national wage figure looks healthy.
segments.tr: Les ménages qui supportent des coûts élevés de loyer, de prêt hypothécaire ou de carte de crédit peuvent toujours se sentir à l'étroit même lorsque le chiffre national des salaires semble sain.

segments.src: ## Job-switching: a sign of confidence, or a fading one
segments.tr: ## Job-switching: a sign of confidence, or a fading one

segments.src: Economists watch how often workers quit voluntarily.
segments.tr: Les économistes observent la fréquence à laquelle les travailleurs démissionnent volontairement.

segments.src: People generally leave a job when they are confident they can find a better one.
segments.tr: Les gens quittent généralement un emploi lorsqu'ils sont convaincus d'en trouver un meilleur.

segments.src: A high quit rate suggests a confident labor market with plenty of openings.
segments.tr: Un taux de démission élevé suggère un marché du travail confiant avec de nombreuses ouvertures.

segments.src: A falling quit rate suggests workers are staying put, and that employers are posting fewer openings.
segments.tr: Un taux de démission en baisse suggère que les travailleurs restent en place et que les employeurs affichent moins d'offres d'emploi.

segments.src: In the past few years, the pace of job-switching has cooled from its peak.
segments.tr: Ces dernières années, le rythme des changements d'emploi a ralenti par rapport à son pic.

segments.src: That has two effects:
segments.tr: Cela a deux effets :

segments.src: - **Less pressure on pay.** When fewer people change jobs, employers feel less need to raise wages to compete.
segments.tr: - **Less pressure on pay.** Lorsque moins de personnes changent d'emploi, les employeurs ressentent moins le besoin d'augmenter les salaires pour rivaliser.

segments.src: - **Harder entry for new job seekers.** Fewer vacancies are created when current employees stay in their roles, which can make it tougher for the unemployed and for people entering the workforce.
segments.tr: - **Harder entry for new job seekers.** Moins de postes vacants sont créés lorsque les employés actuels restent à leur poste, ce qui peut rendre la tâche plus difficile pour les chômeurs et les personnes entrant sur le marché du travail.

segments.src: This helps explain why a strong payroll number and a feeling of "a low-hire, low-fire" job market can both be true at once.
segments.tr: Cela aide à expliquer pourquoi un chiffre d'emploi solide et un sentiment de marché du travail « à faible embauche, faible licenciement » peuvent tous deux être vrais en même temps.

segments.src: ## Why markets read good news as a rate risk
segments.tr: ## Why markets read good news as a rate risk

segments.src: For many people, the most puzzling part of a jobs report day is that stocks or bonds sometimes fall after good news.
segments.tr: Pour beaucoup de gens, la partie la plus déroutante d'un jour de rapport sur l'emploi est que les actions ou les obligations chutent parfois après de bonnes nouvelles.

segments.src: The reason is interest rates.
segments.tr: La raison en est les taux d'intérêt.

segments.src: The Federal Reserve sets its policy rate with two goals in mind: maximum employment and stable prices.
segments.tr: La Réserve fédérale fixe son taux directeur avec deux objectifs en tête : un emploi maximal et des prix stables.

segments.src: When the labor market is strong and wages are rising, the case for lowering rates weakens.
segments.tr: Lorsque le marché du travail est fort et que les salaires augmentent, les arguments en faveur d'une baisse des taux s'affaiblissent.

segments.src: Investors who had been counting on rate cuts may have to change their expectations.
segments.tr: Les investisseurs qui comptaient sur des baisses de taux devront peut-être modifier leurs attentes.

segments.src: Here is how that chain usually works:
segments.tr: Voici comment cette chaîne fonctionne généralement :

segments.src: 1. **A stronger-than-expected report** suggests the economy does not need extra support from lower rates.
segments.tr: 1. **A stronger-than-expected report** suggère que l'économie n'a pas besoin d'un soutien supplémentaire provenant de taux plus bas.

segments.src: 2. **Expectations for rate cuts are pushed back** or reduced.
segments.tr: 2. **Expectations for rate cuts are pushed back** ou réduites.

segments.src: 3. **Government bond yields often rise**, because investors now expect rates to stay higher for longer.
segments.tr: 3. **Government bond yields often rise**, car les investisseurs s'attendent désormais à ce que les taux restent plus élevés plus longtemps.

segments.src: 4. **Higher yields can weigh on stock prices**, particularly for companies that rely on borrowing or whose value depends heavily on future earnings.
segments.tr: 4. **Higher yields can weigh on stock prices**, en particulier pour les entreprises qui dépendent de l'emprunt ou dont la valeur dépend fortement des bénéfices futurs.

segments.src: 5. **Borrowing costs for households stay elevated.** Mortgage rates, auto loans, and credit cards tend to follow broader rate expectations.
segments.tr: 5. **Borrowing costs for households stay elevated.** Les taux hypothécaires, les prêts automobiles et les cartes de crédit ont tendance à suivre les anticipations de taux plus larges.

segments.src: This is why a report can be good for workers and still unwelcome for people hoping for cheaper loans.
segments.tr: C'est pourquoi un rapport peut être bon pour les travailleurs tout en restant mal accueilli par les personnes espérant des prêts moins chers.

segments.src: It also explains why traders often react more to the difference between actual and expected numbers than to the numbers themselves.
segments.tr: Cela explique également pourquoi les traders réagissent souvent davantage à la différence entre les chiffres réels et attendus qu'aux chiffres eux-mêmes.

segments.src: ## What to watch next
segments.tr: ## What to watch next

segments.src: A single month rarely changes the broader direction.
segments.tr: Un seul mois modifie rarement la direction générale.

segments.src: These indicators give a fuller view:
segments.tr: Ces indicateurs donnent une vue plus complète :

segments.src: - **Revisions to prior months**, which can change the story of how strong hiring really was.
segments.tr: - **Revisions to prior months**, qui peuvent modifier l'histoire de la vigueur réelle de l'embauche.

segments.src: - **Average hourly earnings**, to see whether wage growth is speeding up or slowing down.
segments.tr: - **Average hourly earnings**, pour voir si la croissance des salaires s'accélère ou ralentit.

segments.src: - **The labor force participation rate**, which shows whether more people are coming back to look for work.
segments.tr: - **The labor force participation rate**, qui montre si un plus grand nombre de personnes reviennent chercher du travail.

segments.src: - **Job openings and quit rates**, from the monthly JOLTS survey, for a read on employer demand and worker confidence.
segments.tr: - **Job openings and quit rates**, issus de l'enquête mensuelle JOLTS, pour avoir une lecture de la demande des employeurs et de la confiance des travailleurs.

segments.src: - **Weekly jobless claims**, an early signal of layoffs.
segments.tr: - **Weekly jobless claims**, un signal précoce des licenciements.

segments.src: - **Inflation data and Federal Reserve communications**, since these shape how policymakers respond to the labor market.
segments.tr: - **Inflation data and Federal Reserve communications**, car celles-ci façonnent la réaction des décideurs politiques face au marché du travail.

segments.src: ## The bottom line
segments.tr: ## The bottom line

segments.src: A report showing 165,000 new jobs and a 4.1% unemployment rate is, by most measures, evidence of a resilient labor market.
segments.tr: Un rapport montrant 165 000 nouveaux emplois et un taux de chômage de 4,1 % est, à la plupart des égards, la preuve d'un marché du travail résilient.

segments.src: But resilience is not the same as broad-based strength.
segments.tr: Mais la résilience n'est pas synonyme de force généralisée.

segments.src: Gains concentrated in a few industries, uneven results across age groups, and slower job-switching all suggest that many people are not feeling the benefit equally.
segments.tr: Les gains concentrés dans quelques secteurs, les résultats inégaux selon les tranches d'âge et le ralentissement des changements d'emploi suggèrent tous que de nombreuses personnes ne ressentent pas le bénéfice de manière égale.

segments.src: And because strong employment can delay interest rate cuts, good news for the job market can mean a more cautious outlook for borrowers and investors.
segments.tr: Et parce qu'un emploi solide peut retarder les baisses de taux d'intérêt, les bonnes nouvelles pour le marché du travail peuvent signifier des perspectives plus prudentes pour les emprunteurs et les investisseurs.

segments.src: The most useful way to read a jobs report is to look past the headline: ask who is being hired, how much they are paid, and what it means for the path of interest rates.
segments.tr: La manière la plus utile de lire un rapport sur l'emploi est de regarder au-delà du titre : demander qui est embauché, combien ils sont payés et ce que cela signifie pour la trajectoire des taux d'intérêt.

segments.tr: *Les chiffres cités sont ceux rapportés pour octobre et peuvent faire l'objet de révisions.

segments.src: Readers should consult official sources, such as the Bureau of Labor Statistics, for the latest data.
segments.tr: Les lecteurs doivent consulter les sources officielles, telles que le Bureau of Labor Statistics, pour obtenir les dernières données.

pt.title: 165.000 Empregos e 4,1% de Desemprego: Por Que um Relatório Forte de Outubro Não É Uma Boa Notícia para Todos

segments.src: A monthly jobs report is often summed up in a single headline number.
segments.tr: Um relatório mensal de empregos é frequentemente resumido em um único número de destaque.

segments.src: For October, that number was 165,000 jobs added, with the unemployment rate at 4.1%.
segments.tr: Para outubro, esse número foi de 165.000 empregos criados, com a taxa de desemprego em 4,1%.

segments.src: Payrolls came in above what forecasters expected, and on the surface that looks like good news.
segments.tr: A folha de pagamento veio acima do esperado pelos analistas, e, à primeira vista, isso parece uma boa notícia.

segments.src: Look closer and the picture is more mixed.
segments.tr: Olhando mais de perto, o cenário é mais misto.

segments.src: Hiring was uneven across industries and age groups, and financial markets tend to treat a strong labor market as a reason to expect higher borrowing costs for longer.
segments.tr: As contratações foram desiguais entre os setores e faixas etárias, e os mercados financeiros tendem a tratar um mercado de trabalho forte como um motivo para esperar custos de empréstimos mais altos por mais tempo.

segments.src: This article walks through what the figures suggest, why strength for the economy and relief for households and investors are not always the same thing, and which details are worth watching in the months ahead.
segments.tr: Este artigo explica o que os dados sugerem, por que a força da economia e o alívio para as famílias e investidores nem sempre são a mesma coisa, e quais detalhes valem a pena acompanhar nos próximos meses.

segments.tr: *Este artigo destina-se apenas a fins informativos gerais.
