segments.src: ## What the headline numbers say
segments.tr: ## O que os números principais dizem

segments.src: The monthly employment report comes from two separate surveys.
segments.tr: O relatório mensal de emprego vem de duas pesquisas separadas.

segments.src: One asks employers how many people are on their payrolls.
segments.tr: Uma pergunta aos empregadores quantas pessoas estão em suas folhas de pagamento.

segments.src: The other asks households whether they are working or looking for work.
segments.tr: A outra pergunta às famílias se estão trabalhando ou procurando trabalho.

segments.src: The 165,000 figure comes from the employer survey.
segments.tr: O número de 165.000 vem da pesquisa com os empregadores.

segments.src: The 4.1% unemployment rate comes from the household survey.
segments.tr: A taxa de desemprego de 4,1% vem da pesquisa com as famílias.

segments.src: A few points of context help:
segments.tr: Alguns pontos de contexto ajudam:

segments.src: - **165,000 is solid, not spectacular.** In a growing economy, a gain in this range is generally enough to absorb new entrants to the labor force. It is not the kind of surge that signals overheating on its own.
segments.tr: - **165.000 é sólido, não espetacular.** Em uma economia em crescimento, um ganho nessa faixa é geralmente suficiente para absorver os novos ingressantes na força de trabalho. Não é o tipo de surto que sinaliza superaquecimento por si só.

segments.src: - **4.1% is historically low.** By long-run standards, an unemployment rate near 4% is consistent with a tight labor market, where employers compete for workers.
segments.tr: - **4,1% é historicamente baixo.** Para os padrões de longo prazo, uma taxa de desemprego próxima a 4% é consistente com um mercado de trabalho aquecido, onde os empregadores competem por trabalhadores.

segments.src: - **Beating expectations matters in its own right.** Forecasters publish estimates before each report. A result above the consensus is treated as a surprise, and surprises move markets even when the underlying change is modest.
segments.tr: - **Superar as expectativas é importante por si só.** Os analistas publicam estimativas antes de cada relatório. Um resultado acima do consenso é tratado como uma surpresa, e surpresas movimentam os mercados mesmo quando a mudança subjacente é modesta.

segments.src: - **Numbers get revised.** Initial estimates are often adjusted in later months. One report is a snapshot, not a verdict.
segments.tr: - **Os números são revisados.** As estimativas iniciais costumam ser ajustadas nos meses seguintes. Um relatório é um instantâneo, não um veredito definitivo.

segments.src: This helps explain why a strong payroll number and a feeling of "a low-hire, low-fire" job market can both be true at once.
segments.tr: Isso ajuda a explicar por que um número forte na folha de pagamento e a sensação de um mercado de trabalho de "poucas contratações e poucas demissões" podem ser verdadeiros ao mesmo tempo.

segments.src: ## Why markets read good news as a rate risk
segments.tr: ## Por que os mercados veem boas notícias como um risco para as taxas de juros

segments.src: For many people, the most puzzling part of a jobs report day is that stocks or bonds sometimes fall after good news.
segments.tr: Para muitas pessoas, a parte mais intrigante do dia de divulgação do relatório de empregos é que as ações ou títulos às vezes caem após boas notícias.

segments.src: The reason is interest rates.
segments.tr: O motivo são as taxas de juros.

segments.src: The Federal Reserve sets its policy rate with two goals in mind: maximum employment and stable prices.
segments.tr: O Federal Reserve define sua taxa básica com dois objetivos em mente: máximo emprego e preços estáveis.

segments.src: When the labor market is strong and wages are rising, the case for lowering rates weakens.
segments.tr: Quando o mercado de trabalho está forte e os salários estão subindo, os argumentos para reduzir as taxas enfraquecem.

segments.src: Investors who had been counting on rate cuts may have to change their expectations.
segments.tr: Investidores que contavam com cortes nas taxas podem ter que mudar suas expectativas.

segments.src: Here is how that chain usually works:
segments.tr: Veja como essa cadeia geralmente funciona:

segments.src: 1. **A stronger-than-expected report** suggests the economy does not need extra support from lower rates.
segments.tr: 1. **Um relatório mais forte do que o esperado** sugere que a economia não precisa de suporte extra de taxas mais baixas.

segments.src: 2. **Expectations for rate cuts are pushed back** or reduced.
segments.tr: 2. **As expectativas para cortes nas taxas são adiadas** ou reduzidas.

segments.src: 3. **Government bond yields often rise**, because investors now expect rates to stay higher for longer.
segments.tr: 3. **Os rendimentos dos títulos do governo geralmente sobem**, porque os investidores agora esperam que as taxas permaneçam mais altas por mais tempo.

segments.src: 4. **Higher yields can weigh on stock prices**, particularly for companies that rely on borrowing or whose value depends heavily on future earnings.
segments.tr: 4. **Rendimentos mais altos podem pesar sobre os preços das ações**, particularmente de empresas que dependem de empréstimos ou cujo valor depende fortemente de lucros futuros.

segments.src: 5. **Borrowing costs for households stay elevated.** Mortgage rates, auto loans, and credit cards tend to follow broader rate expectations.
segments.tr: 5. **Os custos de empréstimo para as famílias permanecem elevados.** As taxas de hipoteca, empréstimos de veículos e cartões de crédito tendem a seguir as expectativas gerais de juros.

segments.src: This is why a report can be good for workers and still unwelcome for people hoping for cheaper loans.
segments.tr: É por isso que um relatório pode ser bom para os trabalhadores e ainda assim ser indesejado para as pessoas que esperam por empréstimos mais baratos.

segments.src: It also explains why traders often react more to the difference between actual and expected numbers than to the numbers themselves.
segments.tr: Isso também explica por que os operadores frequentemente reagem mais à diferença entre os números reais e esperados do que aos próprios números.

segments.src: ## What to watch next
segments.tr: ## O que observar a seguir

segments.src: A single month rarely changes the broader direction.
segments.tr: Um único mês raramente muda a direção mais ampla.

segments.src: These indicators give a fuller view:
segments.tr: Estes indicadores oferecem uma visão mais completa:

segments.src: - **Revisions to prior months**, which can change the story of how strong hiring really was.
segments.tr: - **Revisões dos meses anteriores**, que podem mudar a história de quão forte realmente foi a contratação.

segments.src: - **Average hourly earnings**, to see whether wage growth is speeding up or slowing down.
segments.tr: - **Ganhos médios por hora**, para ver se o crescimento salarial está acelerando ou desacelerando.

segments.src: - **The labor force participation rate**, which shows whether more people are coming back to look for work.
segments.tr: - **A taxa de participação na força de trabalho**, que mostra se mais pessoas estão voltando a procurar trabalho.

segments.src: - **Job openings and quit rates**, from the monthly JOLTS survey, for a read on employer demand and worker confidence.
segments.tr: - **Vagas abertas e taxas de demissão**, da pesquisa mensal JOLTS, para uma leitura sobre a demanda dos empregadores e a confiança dos trabalhadores.

segments.src: - **Weekly jobless claims**, an early signal of layoffs.
segments.tr: - **Pedidos semanais de auxílio-desemprego**, um sinal antecipado de demissões.

segments.src: - **Inflation data and Federal Reserve communications**, since these shape how policymakers respond to the labor market.
segments.tr: - **Dados de inflação e comunicações do Federal Reserve**, pois estes moldam como os formuladores de políticas respondem ao mercado de trabalho.

segments.src: ## The bottom line
segments.tr: ## A linha final

segments.src: A report showing 165,000 new jobs and a 4.1% unemployment rate is, by most measures, evidence of a resilient labor market.
segments.tr: Um relatório mostrando 165.000 novos empregos e uma taxa de desemprego de 4,1% é, pela maioria das métricas, evidência de um mercado de trabalho resiliente.

segments.src: But resilience is not the same as broad-based strength.
segments.tr: Mas resiliência não é o mesmo que força ampla e generalizada.

segments.src: Gains concentrated in a few industries, uneven results across age groups, and slower job-switching all suggest that many people are not feeling the benefit equally.
segments.tr: Ganhos concentrados em poucos setores, resultados desiguais entre faixas etárias e desaceleração na troca de empregos sugerem que muitas pessoas não estão sentindo o benefício igualmente.

segments.src: And because strong employment can delay interest rate cuts, good news for the job market can mean a more cautious outlook for borrowers and investors.
segments.tr: E como o emprego forte pode adiar os cortes nas taxas de juros, boas notícias para o mercado de trabalho podem significar uma perspectiva mais cautelosa para tomadores de empréstimos e investidores.

segments.src: The most useful way to read a jobs report is to look past the headline: ask who is being hired, how much they are paid, and what it means for the path of interest rates.
segments.tr: A maneira mais útil de ler um relatório de empregos é olhar além da manchete: perguntar quem está sendo contratado, quanto estão recebendo e o que isso significa para a trajetória das taxas de juros.

segments.tr: Os leitores devem consultar fontes oficiais, como o Bureau of Labor Statistics, para obter os dados mais recentes.

in.title: 165.000 Pekerjaan dan Pengangguran 4,1%: Mengapa Laporan Oktober yang Kuat Bukan Berita Baik bagi Semua Orang

segments.src: A monthly jobs report is often summed up in a single headline number.
segments.tr: Laporan pekerjaan bulanan seringkali dirangkum dalam satu angka utama.

segments.src: For October, that number was 165,000 jobs added, with the unemployment rate at 4.1%.
segments.tr: Untuk bulan Oktober, angka tersebut adalah 165.000 penambahan pekerjaan, dengan tingkat pengangguran sebesar 4,1%.

segments.src: Payrolls came in above what forecasters expected, and on the surface that looks like good news.
segments.tr: Jumlah penggajian berada di atas perkiraan para peramal, dan di permukaan hal itu tampak seperti berita bagus.

segments.src: Look closer and the picture is more mixed.
segments.tr: Jika dilihat lebih dekat, situasinya lebih beragam.

segments.src: Hiring was uneven across industries and age groups, and financial markets tend to treat a strong labor market as a reason to expect higher borrowing costs for longer.
segments.tr: Perekrutan tidak merata di berbagai industri dan kelompok usia, dan pasar keuangan cenderung memperlakukan pasar tenaga kerja yang kuat sebagai alasan untuk mengharapkan biaya pinjaman yang lebih tinggi untuk waktu yang lebih lama.

segments.src: This article walks through what the figures suggest, why strength for the economy and relief for households and investors are not always the same thing, and which details are worth watching in the months ahead.
segments.tr: Artikel ini mengulas apa yang disarankan oleh angka-angka tersebut, mengapa kekuatan ekonomi dan kelegaan bagi rumah tangga serta investor tidak selalu merupakan hal yang sama, dan detail mana yang layak diperhatikan dalam beberapa bulan ke depan.

segments.src: *This article is for general information only.
segments.tr: *Artikel ini hanya untuk informasi umum.

segments.src: It is not financial, investment, or employment advice.*
segments.tr: Ini bukan saran keuangan, investasi, atau ketenagakerjaan.*

segments.src: ## What the headline numbers say
segments.tr: ## Apa kata angka utama tersebut

segments.src: The monthly employment report comes from two separate surveys.
segments.tr: Laporan ketenagakerjaan bulanan berasal dari dua survei terpisah.

segments.src: One asks employers how many people are on their payrolls.
segments.tr: Satu survei menanyakan kepada para pemberi kerja berapa banyak orang yang ada dalam daftar gaji mereka.

segments.src: The other asks households whether they are working or looking for work.
segments.tr: Survei lainnya menanyakan kepada rumah tangga apakah mereka sedang bekerja atau sedang mencari pekerjaan.

segments.src: The 165,000 figure comes from the employer survey.
segments.tr: Angka 165.000 berasal dari survei pemberi kerja.

segments.src: The 4.1% unemployment rate comes from the household survey.
segments.tr: Tingkat pengangguran 4,1% berasal dari survei rumah tangga.

segments.src: A few points of context help:
segments.tr: Beberapa poin konteks membantu:

segments.src: - **165,000 is solid, not spectacular.** In a growing economy, a gain in this range is generally enough to absorb new entrants to the labor force. It is not the kind of surge that signals overheating on its own.
segments.tr: - **165.000 itu solid, bukan luar biasa.** Dalam ekonomi yang sedang tumbuh, kenaikan dalam kisaran ini umumnya cukup untuk menyerap pendatang baru ke angkatan kerja. Ini bukan jenis lonjakan yang menandakan overheated dengan sendirinya.

segments.src: - **4.1% is historically low.** By long-run standards, an unemployment rate near 4% is consistent with a tight labor market, where employers compete for workers.
segments.tr: - **4,1% secara historis rendah.** Berdasarkan standar jangka panjang, tingkat pengangguran mendekati 4% konsisten dengan pasar tenaga kerja yang ketat, di mana para pemberi kerja bersaing untuk mendapatkan pekerja.

segments.src: - **Beating expectations matters in its own right.** Forecasters publish estimates before each report. A result above the consensus is treated as a surprise, and surprises move markets even when the underlying change is modest.
segments.tr: - **Mengalahkan ekspektasi itu penting dengan sendirinya.** Para peramal menerbitkan perkiraan sebelum setiap laporan. Hasil di atas konsensus dianggap sebagai kejutan, dan kejutan menggerakkan pasar bahkan ketika perubahan mendasarnya kecil.

segments.src: - **Numbers get revised.** Initial estimates are often adjusted in later months. One report is a snapshot, not a verdict.
segments.tr: - **Angka-angka direvisi.** Perkiraan awal seringkali disesuaikan pada bulan-bulan berikutnya. Satu laporan adalah sebuah snapshot, bukan sebuah putusan.

segments.src: ## Where hiring was strong, and where it wasn't
segments.tr: ## Di mana perekrutan kuat, dan di mana tidak

segments.src: A headline total can hide very different experiences underneath.
segments.tr: Total utama dapat menyembunyikan pengalaman yang sangat berbeda di baliknya.

segments.src: In reports like this one, job gains tend to cluster in a small number of sectors, while others stay flat or shrink.
segments.tr: Dalam laporan seperti ini, kenaikan pekerjaan cenderung berkumpul di sejumlah kecil sektor, sementara yang lain tetap datar atau menyusut.

segments.src: **Industries.** Health care, social assistance, and government have been consistent sources of job growth in recent years, partly because demand for those services is steady and less sensitive to the business cycle.
segments.tr: **Industri.** Perawatan kesehatan, bantuan sosial, dan pemerintah telah menjadi sumber pertumbuhan pekerjaan yang konsisten dalam beberapa tahun terakhir, sebagian karena permintaan untuk layanan tersebut stabil dan tidak terlalu sensitif terhadap siklus bisnis.

segments.src: Sectors that depend more on discretionary spending or interest rates, such as parts of manufacturing, construction, retail, and information technology, have tended to be more volatile.
segments.tr: Sektor yang lebih bergantung pada pengeluaran diskresioner atau tingkat suku bunga, seperti bagian dari manufaktur, konstruksi, ritel, dan teknologi informasi, cenderung lebih mudah berubah.

segments.src: When most of the gains come from a few areas, a strong total can coexist with real weakness elsewhere.
segments.tr: Ketika sebagian besar kenaikan berasal dari beberapa area, total yang kuat dapat berdampingan dengan kelemahan nyata di tempat lain.

segments.src: **Age groups.** Workers in their prime working years, roughly 25 to 54, have had very high employment rates.
segments.tr: **Kelompok usia.** Pekerja di usia prima kerja mereka, sekitar 25 hingga 54 tahun, memiliki tingkat pekerjaan yang sangat tinggi.

segments.src: Younger workers and new graduates often face a harder search when employers slow hiring for entry-level roles.
segments.tr: Pekerja yang lebih muda dan lulusan baru sering kali menghadapi pencarian yang lebih sulit ketika pemberi kerja memperlambat perekrutan untuk peran tingkat pemula.

segments.src: Older workers who lose a job may take longer to find a new one.
segments.tr: Pekerja yang lebih tua yang kehilangan pekerjaan mungkin membutuhkan waktu lebih lama untuk menemukan yang baru.

segments.src: The overall unemployment rate averages all of this out, which is why a good headline can feel out of step with what some job seekers report.
segments.tr: Tingkat pengangguran keseluruhan merata dari semua ini, itulah sebabnya tajuk utama yang baik bisa terasa tidak sejalan dengan apa yang dilaporkan oleh beberapa pencari kerja.

segments.src: **Hours and job quality.** The count of jobs does not show whether positions are full-time, part-time, or temporary.
segments.tr: **Jam kerja dan kualitas pekerjaan.** Penghitungan pekerjaan tidak menunjukkan apakah posisi tersebut penuh waktu, paruh waktu, atau sementara.

segments.src: Analysts also look at average weekly hours and at the share of people working part-time who would prefer full-time work.
segments.tr: Analis juga melihat rata-rata jam kerja mingguan dan pangsa orang yang bekerja paruh waktu yang lebih menyukai pekerjaan penuh waktu.

segments.src: ## Wages: growing, but is it enough?
segments.tr: ## Upah: tumbuh, tetapi apakah itu cukup?

segments.src: Pay is the second half of the story.
segments.tr: Gaji adalah paruh kedua dari cerita ini.

segments.src: When unemployment is low, employers usually have to offer more to attract and keep workers, so wage growth tends to stay firm.
segments.tr: Ketika pengangguran rendah, pemberi kerja biasanya harus menawarkan lebih banyak untuk menarik dan mempertahankan pekerja, sehingga pertumbuhan upah cenderung tetap kuat.

segments.src: That is good news for workers if pay rises faster than prices.
segments.tr: Itu adalah berita bagus bagi pekerja jika gaji naik lebih cepat daripada harga.

segments.src: It is more complicated if inflation has also been running above the central bank's 2% goal.
segments.tr: Lebih rumit jika inflasi juga berjalan di atas target bank sentral sebesar 2%.

segments.src: In that case, solid wage growth can look like a risk to policymakers.
segments.tr: Dalam hal ini, pertumbuhan upah yang solid dapat terlihat seperti risiko bagi para pembuat kebijakan.

segments.src: Their concern is that higher labor costs get passed on through prices, especially in service industries where labor is a large share of the bill.
segments.tr: Kekhawatiran mereka adalah bahwa biaya tenaga kerja yang lebih tinggi diteruskan melalui harga, terutama di industri jasa di mana tenaga kerja merupakan bagian besar dari tagihan.

segments.src: Averages also hide differences.
segments.tr: Rata-rata juga menyembunyikan perbedaan.

segments.src: Workers who change jobs have often received larger raises than those who stay put, while pay increases for people in the same role have been smaller.
segments.tr: Pekerja yang berpindah pekerjaan sering kali menerima kenaikan gaji yang lebih besar daripada mereka yang tetap tinggal, sementara kenaikan gaji untuk orang-orang dalam peran yang sama lebih kecil.

segments.src: Households that carry high rent, mortgage, or credit card costs may still feel stretched even when the national wage figure looks healthy.
segments.tr: Rumah tangga yang menanggung biaya sewa, hipotek, atau kartu kredit yang tinggi mungkin masih merasa tertekan bahkan ketika angka upah nasional terlihat sehat.

segments.src: ## Job-switching: a sign of confidence, or a fading one
segments.tr: ## Perpindahan pekerjaan: tanda kepercayaan diri, atau yang semakin memudar

segments.src: Economists watch how often workers quit voluntarily.
segments.tr: Ekonom mengamati seberapa sering pekerja berhenti secara sukarela.

segments.src: People generally leave a job when they are confident they can find a better one.
segments.tr: Orang umumnya meninggalkan pekerjaan ketika mereka yakin dapat menemukan yang lebih baik.

segments.src: A high quit rate suggests a confident labor market with plenty of openings.
segments.tr: Tingkat pengunduran diri yang tinggi menunjukkan pasar tenaga kerja yang percaya diri dengan banyak lowongan.

segments.src: A falling quit rate suggests workers are staying put, and that employers are posting fewer openings.
segments.tr: Tingkat pengunduran diri yang menurun menunjukkan pekerja tetap tinggal, dan pemberi kerja memasang lebih sedikit lowongan.

segments.src: In the past few years, the pace of job-switching has cooled from its peak.
segments.tr: Dalam beberapa tahun terakhir, kecepatan perpindahan pekerjaan telah dingin dari puncaknya.

segments.src: That has two effects:
segments.tr: Itu memiliki dua efek:

segments.src: - **Less pressure on pay.** When fewer people change jobs, employers feel less need to raise wages to compete.
segments.tr: - **Tekanan lebih sedikit pada gaji.** Ketika lebih sedikit orang yang mengubah pekerjaan, pemberi kerja merasa lebih sedikit kebutuhan untuk menaikkan upah untuk bersaing.

segments.src: - **Harder entry for new job seekers.** Fewer vacancies are created when current employees stay in their roles, which can make it tougher for the unemployed and for people entering the workforce.
segments.tr: - **Masuk yang lebih sulit bagi pencari kerja baru.** Lebih sedikit lowongan yang tercipta ketika karyawan saat ini tetap berada dalam peran mereka, yang dapat membuat segalanya lebih sulit bagi pengangguran dan orang-orang yang memasuki angkatan kerja.

segments.src: This helps explain why a strong payroll number and a feeling of "a low-hire, low-fire" job market can both be true at once.
segments.tr: Ini membantu menjelaskan mengapa angka penggajian yang kuat dan perasaan pasar kerja "sedikit rekrut, sedikit pecat" keduanya bisa benar sekaligus.

segments.src: ## Why markets read good news as a rate risk
segments.tr: ## Mengapa pasar membaca berita bagus sebagai risiko suku bunga

segments.src: For many people, the most puzzling part of a jobs report day is that stocks or bonds sometimes fall after good news.
segments.tr: Bagi banyak orang, bagian paling membingungkan dari hari laporan pekerjaan adalah bahwa saham atau obligasi terkadang turun setelah berita bagus.

segments.src: The reason is interest rates.
segments.tr: Alasannya adalah suku bunga.

segments.src: The Federal Reserve sets its policy rate with two goals in mind: maximum employment and stable prices.
segments.tr: Federal Reserve menetapkan tingkat kebijakannya dengan dua tujuan dalam pikiran: pekerjaan maksimum dan harga yang stabil.

segments.src: When the labor market is strong and wages are rising, the case for lowering rates weakens.
segments.tr: Ketika pasar tenaga kerja kuat dan upah meningkat, alasan untuk menurunkan suku bunga melemah.

segments.src: Investors who had been counting on rate cuts may have to change their expectations.
segments.tr: Investor yang mengandalkan pemotongan suku bunga mungkin harus mengubah ekspektasi mereka.

segments.src: Here is how that chain usually works:
segments.tr: Berikut adalah cara rantai itu biasanya bekerja:

segments.src: 1. **A stronger-than-expected report** suggests the economy does not need extra support from lower rates.
segments.tr: 1. **Laporan yang lebih kuat dari perkiraan** menunjukkan ekonomi tidak memerlukan dukungan tambahan dari suku bunga yang lebih rendah.

segments.src: 2. **Expectations for rate cuts are pushed back** or reduced.
segments.tr: 2. **Ekspektasi untuk pemotongan suku bunga ditunda** atau dikurangi.

segments.src: 3. **Government bond yields often rise**, because investors now expect rates to stay higher for longer.
segments.tr: 3. **Imbal hasil obligasi pemerintah sering naik**, karena investor sekarang mengharapkan suku bunga tetap lebih tinggi untuk waktu yang lebih lama.

segments.src: 4. **Higher yields can weigh on stock prices**, particularly for companies that rely on borrowing or whose value depends heavily on future earnings.
segments.tr: 4. **Imbal hasil yang lebih tinggi dapat membebani harga saham**, terutama bagi perusahaan yang bergantung pada pinjaman atau yang nilainya sangat bergantung pada pendapatan masa depan.

segments.src: 5. **Borrowing costs for households stay elevated.** Mortgage rates, auto loans, and credit cards tend to follow broader rate expectations.
segments.tr: 5. **Biaya pinjaman untuk rumah tangga tetap tinggi.** Suku bunga hipotek, pinjaman mobil, dan kartu kredit cenderung mengikuti ekspektasi suku bunga yang lebih luas.

segments.src: This is why a report can be good for workers and still unwelcome for people hoping for cheaper loans.
segments.tr: Inilah sebabnya mengapa laporan dapat menjadi hal yang baik bagi para pekerja dan masih tidak disambut baik oleh orang-orang yang mengharapkan pinjaman yang lebih murah.

segments.src: It also explains why traders often react more to the difference between actual and expected numbers than to the numbers themselves.
segments.tr: Ini juga menjelaskan mengapa pedagang sering bereaksi lebih banyak terhadap perbedaan antara angka aktual dan yang diharapkan daripada angka itu sendiri.

segments.src: ## What to watch next
segments.tr: ## Apa yang harus diperhatikan selanjutnya

segments.src: A single month rarely changes the broader direction.
segments.tr: Satu bulan jarang mengubah arah yang lebih luas.

segments.src: These indicators give a fuller view:
segments.tr: Indikator-indikator ini memberikan pandangan yang lebih lengkap:

segments.src: - **Revisions to prior months**, which can change the story of how strong hiring really was.
segments.tr: - **Revisi ke bulan-bulan sebelumnya**, yang dapat mengubah cerita tentang seberapa kuat perekrutan sebenarnya.

segments.src: - **Average hourly earnings**, to see whether wage growth is speeding up or slowing down.
segments.tr: - **Penghasilan per jam rata-rata**, untuk melihat apakah pertumbuhan upah semakin cepat atau melambat.

segments.src: - **The labor force participation rate**, which shows whether more people are coming back to look for work.
segments.tr: - **Tingkat partisipasi angkatan kerja**, yang menunjukkan apakah lebih banyak orang kembali untuk mencari pekerjaan.

segments.src: - **Job openings and quit rates**, from the monthly JOLTS survey, for a read on employer demand and worker confidence.
segments.tr: - **Lowongan pekerjaan dan tingkat pengunduran diri**, dari survei JOLTS bulanan, untuk membaca permintaan pengusaha dan kepercayaan pekerja.

segments.src: - **Weekly jobless claims**, an early signal of layoffs.
segments.tr: - **Klaim pengangguran mingguan**, sinyal awal PHK.

segments.src: - **Inflation data and Federal Reserve communications**, since these shape how policymakers respond to the labor market.
segments.tr: - **Data inflasi dan komunikasi Federal Reserve**, karena ini membentuk bagaimana pembuat kebijakan merespons pasar tenaga kerja.

segments.src: ## The bottom line
segments.tr: ## Garis bawah

segments.src: A report showing 165,000 new jobs and a 4.1% unemployment rate is, by most measures, evidence of a resilient labor market.
segments.tr: Sebuah laporan yang menunjukkan 165.000 pekerjaan baru dan tingkat pengangguran 4,1% adalah, dengan sebagian besar ukuran, bukti pasar tenaga kerja yang tangguh.

segments.src: But resilience is not the same as broad-based strength.
segments.tr: Namun ketahanan tidak sama dengan kekuatan berbasis luas.

segments.src: Gains concentrated in a few industries, uneven results across age groups, and slower job-switching all suggest that many people are not feeling the benefit equally.
segments.tr: Keuntungan yang terkonsentrasi di beberapa industri, hasil yang tidak merata di antara kelompok usia, dan perpindahan pekerjaan yang lebih lambat semuanya menunjukkan bahwa banyak orang tidak merasakan manfaatnya secara merata.

segments.src: And because strong employment can delay interest rate cuts, good news for the job market can mean a more cautious outlook for borrowers and investors.
segments.tr: Dan karena pekerjaan yang kuat dapat menunda pemotongan suku bunga, berita bagus untuk pasar tenaga kerja dapat berarti prospek yang lebih hati-hati bagi peminjam dan investor.

segments.src: The most useful way to read a jobs report is to look past the headline: ask who is being hired, how much they are paid, and what it means for the path of interest rates.
segments.tr: Cara paling berguna untuk membaca laporan pekerjaan adalah melihat melewati berita utama: tanyakan siapa yang direkrut, berapa banyak mereka dibayar, dan apa artinya bagi jalur suku bunga.

ja.title: 16.5万件の雇用増と失業率4.1%：好調な10月の雇用統計がすべての人にとって朗報とは言えない理由

segments.src: A monthly jobs report is often summed up in a single headline number.
segments.tr: 月次の雇用統計は、多くの場合、単一の見出しの数値で総括されます。

segments.src: For October, that number was 165,000 jobs added, with the unemployment rate at 4.1%.
segments.tr: 10月の場合、その数値は16万5千人の雇用増であり、失業率は4.1%でした。

segments.src: Payrolls came in above what forecasters expected, and on the surface that looks like good news.
segments.tr: 給与支給者数は予測を上回って着地し、表面上は良いニュースのように見えます。

segments.src: Look closer and the picture is more mixed.
segments.tr: しかし、よく見ると状況はより複雑です。

segments.src: Hiring was uneven across industries and age groups, and financial markets tend to treat a strong labor market as a reason to expect higher borrowing costs for longer.
segments.tr: 採用活動は業界や年齢層によってむらがあり、金融市場は労働市場の強さを、より長期間にわたって借入コストが高止まりする理由と捉える傾向があります。

segments.src: This article walks through what the figures suggest, why strength for the economy and relief for households and investors are not always the same thing, and which details are worth watching in the months ahead.
segments.tr: この記事では、これらの数字が示していること、経済の強さと家計や投資家への安心感が必ずしも一致しない理由、そして今後数カ月で注目すべき詳細について順に見ていきます。

segments.src: *This article is for general information only.
segments.tr: *この記事は一般的な情報提供のみを目的としています。

segments.src: It is not financial, investment, or employment advice.*
segments.tr: 財務、投資、または雇用の助言を構成するものではありません.*

segments.src: ## What the headline numbers say
segments.tr: ## 見出しの数字が語っていること

segments.src: The monthly employment report comes from two separate surveys.
segments.tr: 月次の雇用統計は、2つの異なる調査に基づいています。

segments.src: One asks employers how many people are on their payrolls.
segments.tr: 1つは雇用主に対して従業員数が何人いるかを尋ねるものです。

segments.src: The other asks households whether they are working or looking for work.
segments.tr: もう1つは家計に対して仕事をしているか、仕事を探しているかを尋ねるものです。

segments.src: The 165,000 figure comes from the employer survey.
segments.tr: 165,000という数値は雇用主調査から得られたものです。

segments.src: The 4.1% unemployment rate comes from the household survey.
segments.tr: 4.1%の失業率は家計調査から得られたものです。

segments.src: A few points of context help:
segments.tr: 背景を理解するためのいくつかのポイント：

segments.src: - **165,000 is solid, not spectacular.** In a growing economy, a gain in this range is generally enough to absorb new entrants to the labor force. It is not the kind of surge that signals overheating on its own.
segments.tr: - **165,000は堅調であるが、驚異的ではない。** 成長している経済において、この範囲の増加は一般的に労働市場への新規参入者を吸収するのに十分な水準です。それ単体で過熱を示唆するような急増ではありません。

segments.src: - **4.1% is historically low.** By long-run standards, an unemployment rate near 4% is consistent with a tight labor market, where employers compete for workers.
segments.tr: - **4.1%は歴史的な低水準である。** 長期的な基準で見ると、4%近い失業率は、雇用主が労働者を求めて競い合う引き締まった労働市場と一致しています。

segments.src: - **Beating expectations matters in its own right.** Forecasters publish estimates before each report. A result above the consensus is treated as a surprise, and surprises move markets even when the underlying change is modest.
segments.tr: - **予想を上回ることに独自の意味がある。** 予測者は各報告の前に推定値を発表します。市場予想を上回る結果はサプライズとして扱われ、根本的な変化が穏やかであっても、サプライズは市場を動かします。

segments.src: - **Numbers get revised.** Initial estimates are often adjusted in later months. One report is a snapshot, not a verdict.
segments.tr: - **数字は修正される。** 当初の推定値は、その後の数カ月で調整されることがよくあります。1つの報告はスナップショットであり、最終的な判決ではありません。

segments.src: ## Where hiring was strong, and where it wasn't
segments.tr: ## 採用が好調だった分野と、そうでない分野

segments.src: A headline total can hide very different experiences underneath.
segments.tr: 見出しの合計値は、その裏にある非常に異なる状況を隠してしまうことがあります。

segments.src: In reports like this one, job gains tend to cluster in a small number of sectors, while others stay flat or shrink.
segments.tr: 今回のような報告では、雇用の伸びが少数のセクターに集中する傾向がある一方で、他のセクターは横ばいか縮小します。

segments.src: **Industries.** Health care, social assistance, and government have been consistent sources of job growth in recent years, partly because demand for those services is steady and less sensitive to the business cycle.
segments.tr: **産業。** ヘルスケア、社会福祉、および政府部門は、近年一貫して雇用の伸びの源泉となっており、その理由の一部は、それらのサービスの需要が安定しており、景気循環の影響を受けにくいためです。

segments.src: Sectors that depend more on discretionary spending or interest rates, such as parts of manufacturing, construction, retail, and information technology, have tended to be more volatile.
segments.tr: 裁量支出や金利により依存しているセクター（製造業の一部、建設、小売、情報技術など）は、より変動しやすい傾向があります。

segments.src: When most of the gains come from a few areas, a strong total can coexist with real weakness elsewhere.
segments.tr: 増加の大半が少数の分野から生じている場合、好調な合計値と、他の場所での現実的な弱さが共存することになります。

segments.src: **Age groups.** Workers in their prime working years, roughly 25 to 54, have had very high employment rates.
segments.tr: **年齢層。** 働き盛りの年齢層、およそ25歳から54歳の労働者は、非常に高い雇用率を維持しています。

segments.src: Younger workers and new graduates often face a harder search when employers slow hiring for entry-level roles.
segments.tr: 若い労働者や新卒者は、雇用主がエントリーレベルの職の採用を鈍らせると、より困難な職探しに直面することがよくあります。

segments.src: Older workers who lose a job may take longer to find a new one.
segments.tr: 職を失った高齢労働者は、新しい仕事を見つけるのに時間がかかる場合があります。

segments.src: The overall unemployment rate averages all of this out, which is why a good headline can feel out of step with what some job seekers report.
segments.tr: 全体の失業率はこれらすべてを平均化するため、良好な見出しが一部の求職者が報告する状況と噛み合わないように感じられる理由がここにあります。

segments.src: **Hours and job quality.** The count of jobs does not show whether positions are full-time, part-time, or temporary.
segments.tr: **労働時間と雇用の質。** 雇用の数では、そのポジションがフルタイム、パートタイム、または一時的なものであるかどうかは示されません。

segments.src: Analysts also look at average weekly hours and at the share of people working part-time who would prefer full-time work.
segments.tr: アナリストはまた、平均週労働時間や、フルタイムでの勤務を希望しながらパートタイムで働いている人の割合にも注目しています。

segments.src: ## Wages: growing, but is it enough?
segments.tr: ## 賃金：上昇しているが、それは十分か？

segments.src: Pay is the second half of the story.
segments.tr: 給与は物語の後半部分です。

segments.src: When unemployment is low, employers usually have to offer more to attract and keep workers, so wage growth tends to stay firm.
segments.tr: 失業率が低い場合、雇用主は労働者を惹きつけ維持するために通常より多くを提示しなければならないため、賃金の伸びはしっかりとしたものにとどまる傾向があります。

segments.src: That is good news for workers if pay rises faster than prices.
segments.tr: 給与が物価よりも速く上昇する場合、それは労働者にとって朗報です。

segments.src: It is more complicated if inflation has also been running above the central bank's 2% goal.
segments.tr: インフレ率が中央銀行の目標である2%を上回って推移している場合、状況はより複雑になります。

segments.src: In that case, solid wage growth can look like a risk to policymakers.
segments.tr: その場合、堅調な賃金の伸びは政策担当者にとってリスクのように映る可能性があります。

segments.src: Their concern is that higher labor costs get passed on through prices, especially in service industries where labor is a large share of the bill.
segments.tr: 彼らの懸念は、労働コストの上昇が物価を通じて転嫁されることであり、特に労働がコストの大きな割合を占めるサービス産業においてそれが顕著になります。

segments.src: Averages also hide differences.
segments.tr: 平均値はまた、差異を隠してしまいます。

segments.src: Workers who change jobs have often received larger raises than those who stay put, while pay increases for people in the same role have been smaller.
segments.tr: 転職した労働者は、同じ職にとどまる労働者よりも大きな昇給を受けていることが多い一方で、同じ役割にいる人々の給与増加は小さくなっています。

segments.src: Households that carry high rent, mortgage, or credit card costs may still feel stretched even when the national wage figure looks healthy.
segments.tr: 高い家賃、住宅ローン、またはクレジットカードのコストを抱える家計は、全国の賃金統計が健全に見えるときでも、依然として家計が圧迫されていると感じるかもしれません。

segments.src: ## Job-switching: a sign of confidence, or a fading one
segments.tr: ## 転職：自信の表れか、それとも薄れゆく兆候か

segments.src: Economists watch how often workers quit voluntarily.
segments.tr: エコノミストは、労働者が自発的に離職する頻度を注視しています。

segments.src: People generally leave a job when they are confident they can find a better one.
segments.tr: 人々は一般的に、より良い仕事を見つけられるという自信があるときに仕事を辞めます。

segments.src: A high quit rate suggests a confident labor market with plenty of openings.
segments.tr: 高い離職率は、求人の豊富な自信に満ちた労働市場を示唆しています。

segments.src: A falling quit rate suggests workers are staying put, and that employers are posting fewer openings.
segments.tr: 低下する離職率は、労働者が現在の職にとどまっており、雇用主が求人を減らしていることを示唆しています。

segments.src: In the past few years, the pace of job-switching has cooled from its peak.
segments.tr: ここ数年、転職のペースはピークから冷却化しています。

segments.src: That has two effects:
segments.tr: それは2つの影響をもたらします：

segments.src: - **Less pressure on pay.** When fewer people change jobs, employers feel less need to raise wages to compete.
segments.tr: - **賃金へのプレッシャーの軽減。** 転職する人が少なくなると、雇用主は競争のために賃金を上げる必要性をあまり感じなくなります。

segments.src: - **Harder entry for new job seekers.** Fewer vacancies are created when current employees stay in their roles, which can make it tougher for the unemployed and for people entering the workforce.
segments.tr: - **新規求職者にとっての参入の困難化。** 現役従業員がその役割にとどまると創出される求人が少なくなり、失業者や労働市場に参入する人々にとって状況がより厳しくなる可能性があります。

segments.src: This helps explain why a strong payroll number and a feeling of "a low-hire, low-fire" job market can both be true at once.
segments.tr: これは、堅調な雇用者数と、「採用少なく解雇も少ない」労働市場という感覚が同時に成立し得る理由を説明するのに役立ちます。

segments.src: ## Why markets read good news as a rate risk
segments.tr: ## 市場が好材料を利下げリスクと捉える理由

segments.src: For many people, the most puzzling part of a jobs report day is that stocks or bonds sometimes fall after good news.
segments.tr: 多くの人にとって、雇用統計発表日に最も不可解な点は、好材料の後に株や債券が下落することがあるということです。

segments.src: The reason is interest rates.
segments.tr: その理由は金利です。

segments.src: The Federal Reserve sets its policy rate with two goals in mind: maximum employment and stable prices.
segments.tr: 米連邦準備制度（FRB）は、最大雇用と物価安定という2つの目標を念頭に置いて政策金利を設定しています。

segments.src: When the labor market is strong and wages are rising, the case for lowering rates weakens.
segments.tr: 労働市場が好調で賃金が上昇しているとき、利下げを行う根拠は弱まります。

segments.src: Investors who had been counting on rate cuts may have to change their expectations.
segments.tr: 利下げを当てにしていた投資家は、期待を変更せざるを得なくなるかもしれません。

segments.src: Here is how that chain usually works:
segments.tr: その連鎖は通常、次のように機能します：

segments.src: 1. **A stronger-than-expected report** suggests the economy does not need extra support from lower rates.
segments.tr: 1. **予想を上回る報告**は、経済が低金利による追加の支援を必要としていないことを示唆します。

segments.src: 2. **Expectations for rate cuts are pushed back** or reduced.
segments.tr: 2. **利下げへの期待が後退する**、または縮小します。

segments.src: 3. **Government bond yields often rise**, because investors now expect rates to stay higher for longer.
segments.tr: 3. **国債利回りが上昇することが多い**。投資家が金利のより長期間の高止まりを予想するようになるためです。

segments.src: 4. **Higher yields can weigh on stock prices**, particularly for companies that rely on borrowing or whose value depends heavily on future earnings.
segments.tr: 4. **利回りの上昇は株価の重荷となる可能性がある**。特に借入に依存している企業や、将来の利益に価値が大きく依存している企業にとってそうです。

segments.src: 5. **Borrowing costs for households stay elevated.** Mortgage rates, auto loans, and credit cards tend to follow broader rate expectations.
segments.tr: 5. **家計の借入コストが高止まりする。** 住宅ローン、自動車ローン、クレジットカードは、より広範な金利予想に追随する傾向があります。

segments.src: This is why a report can be good for workers and still unwelcome for people hoping for cheaper loans.
segments.tr: これが、報告が労働者にとってはプラスであっても、より安価なローンを望む人々にとっては歓迎されない理由です。

segments.src: It also explains why traders often react more to the difference between actual and expected numbers than to the numbers themselves.
segments.tr: また、トレーダーが実際の数値と予想された数値の差に対して、数値そのものよりも強く反応することが多い理由をも説明しています。

segments.src: ## What to watch next
segments.tr: ## 次に注目すべき点

segments.src: A single month rarely changes the broader direction.
segments.tr: たった1カ月で、より大きな方向性が変わることはめったにありません。

segments.src: These indicators give a fuller view:
segments.tr: これらの指標は、より完全な全体像を与えてくれます：

segments.src: - **Revisions to prior months**, which can change the story of how strong hiring really was.
segments.tr: - **前月分の修正**。実際の採用がどれほど強かったかというストーリーを変える可能性があります。

segments.src: - **Average hourly earnings**, to see whether wage growth is speeding up or slowing down.
segments.tr: - **平均時給**。賃金の伸びが加速しているか、減速しているかを確認するため。

segments.src: - **The labor force participation rate**, which shows whether more people are coming back to look for work.
segments.tr: - **労働参加率**。より多くの人々が仕事探しに戻ってきているかどうかを示します。

segments.src: - **Job openings and quit rates**, from the monthly JOLTS survey, for a read on employer demand and worker confidence.
segments.tr: - **求人件数と離職率**。毎月のJOLTS調査から、雇用主の需要と労働者の自信を読み取るため。

segments.src: - **Weekly jobless claims**, an early signal of layoffs.
segments.tr: - **週次新規失業保険申請件数**。レイオフの初期シグナル。

segments.src: - **Inflation data and Federal Reserve communications**, since these shape how policymakers respond to the labor market.
segments.tr: - **インフレデータと米連邦準備制度のコミュニケーション**。これらが政策担当者が労働市場にどう対応するかを形作るため。

segments.src: ## The bottom line
segments.tr: ## 結論

segments.src: A report showing 165,000 new jobs and a 4.1% unemployment rate is, by most measures, evidence of a resilient labor market.
segments.tr: 16万5千人の新規雇用と4.1%の失業率を示す報告は、ほとんどの基準において、回復力のある労働市場の証拠です。

segments.src: But resilience is not the same as broad-based strength.
segments.tr: しかし、回復力は広範な強さと同義ではありません。

segments.src: Gains concentrated in a few industries, uneven results across age groups, and slower job-switching all suggest that many people are not feeling the benefit equally.
segments.tr: 少数の産業に集中した増加、年齢層ごとの不均一な結果、およびより緩やかな転職はすべて、多くの人々がその恩恵を等しく感じていないことを示唆しています。

segments.src: And because strong employment can delay interest rate cuts, good news for the job market can mean a more cautious outlook for borrowers and investors.
segments.tr: そして、好調な雇用は利下げを遅らせる可能性があるため、労働市場にとっての朗報は、借入人や投資家にとってより慎重な見通しを意味することになります。

segments.src: The most useful way to read a jobs report is to look past the headline: ask who is being hired, how much they are paid, and what it means for the path of interest rates.
segments.tr: 雇用統計を読み解く最も有益な方法は、見出しの先を見ることにあります：誰が採用されているのか、いくら支払われているのか、そしてそれが金利の道筋にとって何を意味するのかを問うことです。

segments.src: *Figures cited are as reported for October and may be revised.
segments.tr: *言及されている数値は10月時点の報告に基づくものであり、修正される可能性があります。

segments.src: Readers should consult official sources, such as the Bureau of Labor Statistics, for the latest data.
segments.tr: 読者は最新のデータを得るために、労働統計局などの公式情報源を参照すべきです。

segments.tr: このコンテンツは情報提供のみを目的としており、財務上の助言を構成するものではありません。*

segments.tr: Der Wert von 165.000 stammt aus der Arbeitgeberbefragung.

segments.src: The 4.1% unemployment rate comes from the household survey.
segments.tr: Die Arbeitslosenquote von 4,1 % stammt aus der Haushaltsbefragung.

segments.src: A few points of context help:
segments.tr: Einige Kontextpunkte sind hilfreich:

segments.src: - **165,000 is solid, not spectacular.** In a growing economy, a gain in this range is generally enough to absorb new entrants to the labor force. It is not the kind of surge that signals overheating on its own.
segments.tr: - **165.000 ist solide, nicht spektakulär.** In einer wachsenden Wirtschaft reicht ein Zuwachs in diesem Bereich im Allgemeinen aus, um neue Arbeitskräfte aufzunehmen. Es ist nicht die Art von Aufschwung, die von sich aus eine Überhitzung signalisiert.

segments.src: - **4.1% is historically low.** By long-run standards, an unemployment rate near 4% is consistent with a tight labor market, where employers compete for workers.
segments.tr: - **4,1 % ist historisch niedrig.** Nach langfristigen Maßstäben ist eine Arbeitslosenquote von nahe 4 % vereinbar mit einem angespannten Arbeitsmarkt, auf dem Arbeitgeber um Arbeitskräfte konkurrieren.

segments.src: - **Beating expectations matters in its own right.** Forecasters publish estimates before each report. A result above the consensus is treated as a surprise, and surprises move markets even when the underlying change is modest.
segments.tr: - **Das Übertreffen von Erwartungen ist wichtig an sich.** Prognostiker veröffentlichen Schätzungen vor jedem Bericht. Ein Ergebnis über dem Konsens wird als Überraschung gewertet, und Überraschungen bewegen die Märkte, selbst wenn die zugrundeliegende Veränderung bescheiden ist.

segments.src: - **Numbers get revised.** Initial estimates are often adjusted in later months. One report is a snapshot, not a verdict.
segments.tr: - **Zahlen werden revidiert.** Erste Schätzungen werden in den folgenden Monaten oft angepasst. Ein Bericht ist eine Momentaufnahme, kein endgültiges Urteil.

segments.src: ## Where hiring was strong, and where it wasn't
segments.tr: ## Wo Einstellungen stark waren und wo nicht

segments.src: A headline total can hide very different experiences underneath.
segments.tr: Eine Gesamtzahl in der Schlagzeile kann sehr unterschiedliche Entwicklungen im Hintergrund verbergen.

segments.src: In reports like this one, job gains tend to cluster in a small number of sectors, while others stay flat or shrink.
segments.tr: In Berichten wie diesem neigen Beschäftigungszuwächse dazu, sich in einer kleinen Anzahl von Sektoren zu ballen, während andere stagnieren oder schrumpfen.

segments.src: **Industries.** Health care, social assistance, and government have been consistent sources of job growth in recent years, partly because demand for those services is steady and less sensitive to the business cycle.
segments.tr: **Branchen.** Das Gesundheitswesen, die Sozialhilfe und der öffentliche Sektor waren in den letzten Jahren konstante Quellen des Beschäftigungswachstums, teilweise weil die Nachfrage nach diesen Dienstleistungen stabil und weniger konjunkturabhängig ist.

segments.src: Sectors that depend more on discretionary spending or interest rates, such as parts of manufacturing, construction, retail, and information technology, have tended to be more volatile.
segments.tr: Sektoren, die stärker von diskretionären Ausgaben oder Zinssätzen abhängen – wie Teile des verarbeitenden Gewerbes, das Baugewerbe, der Einzelhandel und die Informationstechnologie –, neigen zu größerer Volatilität.

segments.src: When most of the gains come from a few areas, a strong total can coexist with real weakness elsewhere.
segments.tr: Wenn die meisten Zuwächse aus wenigen Bereichen kommen, kann eine starke Gesamtzahl neben realer Schwäche anderswo existieren.

segments.src: **Age groups.** Workers in their prime working years, roughly 25 to 54, have had very high employment rates.
segments.tr: **Altersgruppen.** Arbeitnehmer in ihren besten Berufsjahren, grob gesagt zwischen 25 und 54 Jahren, hatten sehr hohe Beschäftigungsquoten.

segments.src: Younger workers and new graduates often face a harder search when employers slow hiring for entry-level roles.
segments.tr: Jüngere Arbeitnehmer und neue Absolventen haben oft eine schwierigere Suche, wenn Arbeitgeber Einstellungen für Einstiegspositionen verlangsamen.

segments.src: Older workers who lose a job may take longer to find a new one.
segments.tr: Ältere Arbeitnehmer, die ihren Job verlieren, brauchen möglicherweise länger, um einen neuen zu finden.

segments.src: The overall unemployment rate averages all of this out, which is why a good headline can feel out of step with what some job seekers report.
segments.tr: Die Gesamtarbeitslosenquote mittelt all dies heraus, weshalb sich eine gute Schlagzeile möglicherweise nicht stimmig anfühlt im Vergleich zu dem, was manche Arbeitssuchende berichten.

segments.src: **Hours and job quality.** The count of jobs does not show whether positions are full-time, part-time, or temporary.
segments.tr: **Arbeitsstunden und Jobqualität.** Die Anzahl der Arbeitsplätze zeigt nicht, ob die Positionen Vollzeit-, Teilzeit- oder befristete Jobs sind.

segments.src: Analysts also look at average weekly hours and at the share of people working part-time who would prefer full-time work.
segments.tr: Analysten betrachten auch die durchschnittlichen wöchentlichen Arbeitsstunden und den Anteil von Menschen in Teilzeitarbeit, die eine Vollzeitbeschäftigung bevorzugen würden.

segments.src: ## Wages: growing, but is it enough?
segments.tr: ## Löhne: wachsend, aber ist das genug?

segments.src: Pay is the second half of the story.
segments.tr: Die Bezahlung ist die zweite Hälfte der Geschichte.

segments.src: When unemployment is low, employers usually have to offer more to attract and keep workers, so wage growth tends to stay firm.
segments.tr: Wenn die Arbeitslosigkeit niedrig ist, müssen Arbeitgeber normalerweise mehr anbieten, um Arbeitnehmer anzuziehen und zu halten, weshalb das Lohnwachstum tendenziell robust bleibt.

segments.src: That is good news for workers if pay rises faster than prices.
segments.tr: Das ist eine gute Nachricht für Arbeitnehmer, wenn die Bezahlung schneller steigt als die Preise.

segments.src: It is more complicated if inflation has also been running above the central bank's 2% goal.
segments.tr: Es ist komplizierter, wenn die Inflation ebenfalls über dem 2-%-Ziel der Zentralbank lag.

segments.src: In that case, solid wage growth can look like a risk to policymakers.
segments.tr: In diesem Fall kann ein solides Lohnwachstum für politische Entscheidungsträger wie ein Risiko aussehen.

segments.src: Their concern is that higher labor costs get passed on through prices, especially in service industries where labor is a large share of the bill.
segments.tr: Ihre Sorge ist, dass höhere Arbeitskosten über die Preise weitergegeben werden, insbesondere im Dienstleistungssektor, wo die Arbeit einen großen Teil der Kosten ausmacht.

segments.src: Averages also hide differences.
segments.tr: Durchschnitte verbergen auch Unterschiede.

segments.src: Workers who change jobs have often received larger raises than those who stay put, while pay increases for people in the same role have been smaller.
segments.tr: Arbeitnehmer, die den Job wechseln, haben oft größere Gehaltserhöhungen erhalten als diejenigen, die bleiben, während Gehaltserhöhungen für Personen in derselben Rolle geringer ausfielen.

segments.src: Households that carry high rent, mortgage, or credit card costs may still feel stretched even when the national wage figure looks healthy.
segments.tr: Haushalte, die hohe Miet-, Hypotheken- oder Kreditkartenkosten tragen, fühlen sich möglicherweise weiterhin unter Druck, selbst wenn die nationale Lohnzahl gesund aussieht.

segments.src: ## Job-switching: a sign of confidence, or a fading one
segments.tr: ## Jobwechsel: Ein Zeichen von Zuversicht oder eine schwindende Zuversicht

segments.src: Economists watch how often workers quit voluntarily.
segments.tr: Ökonomen beobachten, wie oft Arbeitnehmer freiwillig kündigen.

segments.src: People generally leave a job when they are confident they can find a better one.
segments.tr: Menschen verlassen einen Job im Allgemeinen, wenn sie zuversichtlich sind, einen besseren finden zu können.

segments.src: A high quit rate suggests a confident labor market with plenty of openings.
segments.tr: Eine hohe Kündigungsrate deutet auf einen zuversichtlichen Arbeitsmarkt mit vielen offenen Stellen hin.

segments.src: A falling quit rate suggests workers are staying put, and that employers are posting fewer openings.
segments.tr: Eine sinkende Kündigungsrate deutet darauf hin, dass Arbeitnehmer bleiben, wo sie sind, und dass Arbeitgeber weniger offene Stellen ausschreiben.

segments.src: In the past few years, the pace of job-switching has cooled from its peak.
segments.tr: In den letzten Jahren hat sich das Tempo der Jobwechsel von seinem Höchststand abgekühlt.

segments.src: That has two effects:
segments.tr: Das hat zwei Effekte:

segments.src: - **Less pressure on pay.** When fewer people change jobs, employers feel less need to raise wages to compete.
segments.tr: - **Weniger Druck auf die Löhne.** Wenn weniger Menschen den Job wechseln, sehen Arbeitgeber weniger Notwendigkeit, die Löhne zur Konkurrenz zu erhöhen.

segments.src: - **Harder entry for new job seekers.** Fewer vacancies are created when current employees stay in their roles, which can make it tougher for the unemployed and for people entering the workforce.
segments.tr: - **Schwierigerer Einstieg für neue Arbeitssuchende.** Es entstehen weniger freie Stellen, wenn aktuelle Mitarbeiter in ihren Rollen bleiben, was es für Arbeitslose und Berufseinsteiger schwieriger machen kann.

segments.src: This helps explain why a strong payroll number and a feeling of "a low-hire, low-fire" job market can both be true at once.
segments.tr: Dies trägt dazu bei zu erklären, warum eine starke Beschäftigungszahl und das Gefühl eines Arbeitsmarktes mit „wenigen Einstellungen, wenigen Entlassungen“ gleichzeitig wahr sein können.

segments.src: ## Why markets read good news as a rate risk
segments.tr: ## Warum Märkte gute Nachrichten als Zinsrisiko interpretieren

segments.src: For many people, the most puzzling part of a jobs report day is that stocks or bonds sometimes fall after good news.
segments.tr: Für viele Menschen ist der rätselhafteste Teil eines Tages mit Arbeitsmarktdaten, dass Aktien oder Anleihen nach guten Nachrichten manchmal fallen.

segments.src: The reason is interest rates.
segments.tr: Der Grund dafür sind Zinssätze.

segments.src: The Federal Reserve sets its policy rate with two goals in mind: maximum employment and stable prices.
segments.tr: Die US-Notenbank Federal Reserve legt ihren Leitzins mit zwei Zielen im Blick fest: maximale Beschäftigung und Preisstabilität.

segments.src: When the labor market is strong and wages are rising, the case for lowering rates weakens.
segments.tr: Wenn der Arbeitsmarkt stark ist und die Löhne steigen, schwächt sich das Argument für Zinssenkungen ab.

segments.src: Investors who had been counting on rate cuts may have to change their expectations.
segments.tr: Investoren, die mit Zinssenkungen gerechnet hatten, müssen möglicherweise ihre Erwartungen ändern.

segments.src: Here is how that chain usually works:
segments.tr: Hier ist, wie diese Kette normalerweise funktioniert:

segments.src: 1. **A stronger-than-expected report** suggests the economy does not need extra support from lower rates.
segments.tr: 1. **Ein stärker als erwarteter Bericht** deutet darauf hin, dass die Wirtschaft keine zusätzliche Unterstützung durch niedrigere Zinsen benötigt.

segments.src: 2. **Expectations for rate cuts are pushed back** or reduced.
segments.tr: 2. **Erwartungen für Zinssenkungen werden nach hinten verschoben** oder reduziert.

segments.src: 3. **Government bond yields often rise**, because investors now expect rates to stay higher for longer.
segments.tr: 3. **Staatsanleihenrenditen steigen oft**, weil Investoren nun erwarten, dass die Zinsen länger höher bleiben.

segments.src: 4. **Higher yields can weigh on stock prices**, particularly for companies that rely on borrowing or whose value depends heavily on future earnings.
segments.tr: 4. **Höhere Renditen können auf Aktienkurse drücken**, insbesondere bei Unternehmen, die auf Kreditaufnahme angewiesen sind oder deren Wert stark von zukünftigen Gewinnen abhängt.

segments.src: 5. **Borrowing costs for households stay elevated.** Mortgage rates, auto loans, and credit cards tend to follow broader rate expectations.
segments.tr: 5. **Die Kreditkosten für Haushalte bleiben erhöht.** Hypothekenzinsen, Autokredite und Kreditkarten neigen dazu, den breiteren Zinserwartungen zu folgen.

segments.src: This is why a report can be good for workers and still unwelcome for people hoping for cheaper loans.
segments.tr: Aus diesem Grund kann ein Bericht für Arbeitnehmer gut und gleichzeitig für Personen, die auf günstigere Kredite hoffen, unerwünscht sein.

segments.src: It also explains why traders often react more to the difference between actual and expected numbers than to the numbers themselves.
segments.tr: Er erklärt auch, warum Händler oft stärker auf die Differenz zwischen tatsächlichen und erwarteten Zahlen reagieren als auf die Zahlen selbst.

segments.src: ## What to watch next
segments.tr: ## Was als Nächstes zu beobachten ist

segments.src: A single month rarely changes the broader direction.
segments.tr: Ein einzelner Monat ändert selten die breitere Richtung.

segments.src: These indicators give a fuller view:
segments.tr: Diese Indikatoren geben einen vollständigeren Blick:

segments.src: - **Revisions to prior months**, which can change the story of how strong hiring really was.
segments.tr: - **Revisionen für Vormonate**, die die Geschichte darüber verändern können, wie stark die Einstellungen wirklich waren.

segments.src: - **Average hourly earnings**, to see whether wage growth is speeding up or slowing down.
segments.tr: - **Durchschnittliche Stundenlöhne**, um zu sehen, ob sich das Lohnwachstum beschleunigt oder verlangsamt.

segments.src: - **The labor force participation rate**, which shows whether more people are coming back to look for work.
segments.tr: - **Die Erwerbsquote**, die zeigt, ob mehr Menschen zurückkehren, um Arbeit zu suchen.

segments.src: - **Job openings and quit rates**, from the monthly JOLTS survey, for a read on employer demand and worker confidence.
segments.tr: - **Offene Stellen und Kündigungsraten** aus der monatlichen JOLTS-Umfrage als Indikator für die Arbeitgebernachfrage und die Zuversicht der Arbeitnehmer.

segments.src: - **Weekly jobless claims**, an early signal of layoffs.
segments.tr: - **Wöchentliche Erstanträge auf Arbeitslosenhilfe**, ein frühes Signal für Entlassungen.

segments.src: - **Inflation data and Federal Reserve communications**, since these shape how policymakers respond to the labor market.
segments.tr: - **Inflationsdaten und die Kommunikation der Federal Reserve**, da diese prägen, wie politische Entscheidungsträger auf den Arbeitsmarkt reagieren.

segments.src: ## The bottom line
segments.tr: ## Das Fazit

segments.src: A report showing 165,000 new jobs and a 4.1% unemployment rate is, by most measures, evidence of a resilient labor market.
segments.tr: Ein Bericht, der 165.000 neue Arbeitsplätze und eine Arbeitslosenquote von 4,1 % zeigt, ist nach den meisten Maßstäben ein Beweis für einen widerstandsfähigen Arbeitsmarkt.

segments.src: But resilience is not the same as broad-based strength.
segments.tr: Aber Widerstandsfähigkeit ist nicht dasselbe wie eine breite Stärke.

segments.src: Gains concentrated in a few industries, uneven results across age groups, and slower job-switching all suggest that many people are not feeling the benefit equally.
segments.tr: Zuwächse, die sich auf wenige Branchen konzentrieren, ungleiche Ergebnisse über Altersgruppen hinweg und langsamere Jobwechsel deuten alle darauf hin, dass viele Menschen den Nutzen nicht gleichermaßen spüren.

segments.src: And because strong employment can delay interest rate cuts, good news for the job market can mean a more cautious outlook for borrowers and investors.
segments.tr: Und weil eine starke Beschäftigung Zinssenkungen verzögern kann, können gute Nachrichten für den Arbeitsmarkt einen vorsichtigeren Ausblick für Kreditnehmer und Investoren bedeuten.

segments.src: The most useful way to read a jobs report is to look past the headline: ask who is being hired, how much they are paid, and what it means for the path of interest rates.
segments.tr: Der nützlichste Weg, einen Arbeitsmarktbericht zu lesen, besteht darin, über die Schlagzeile hinauszublicken: Fragen Sie, wer eingestellt wird, wie viel sie bezahlt bekommen und was es für den Zinspfad bedeutet.

segments.tr: *Die angeführten Zahlen entsprechen den Berichten für Oktober und können revidiert werden.

segments.tr: Leser sollten offizielle Quellen wie das Bureau of Labor Statistics für die neuesten Daten konsultieren.

segments.src: ## What the headline numbers say
segments.tr: ## Các con số tiêu đề nói lên điều gì

segments.src: The monthly employment report comes from two separate surveys.
segments.tr: Báo cáo việc làm hàng tháng đến từ hai cuộc khảo sát riêng biệt.

segments.src: One asks employers how many people are on their payrolls.
segments.tr: Một cuộc hỏi các nhà tuyển dụng xem có bao nhiêu người trong bảng lương của họ.

segments.src: The other asks households whether they are working or looking for work.
segments.tr: Cuộc khảo sát còn lại hỏi các hộ gia đình xem họ đang làm việc hay đang tìm việc.

segments.src: The 165,000 figure comes from the employer survey.
segments.tr: Con số 165.000 đến từ cuộc khảo sát nhà tuyển dụng.

segments.src: The 4.1% unemployment rate comes from the household survey.
segments.tr: Tỷ lệ thất nghiệp 4,1% đến từ cuộc khảo sát hộ gia đình.

segments.src: A few points of context help:
segments.tr: Một vài điểm bối cảnh giúp ích:

segments.src: - **165,000 is solid, not spectacular.** In a growing economy, a gain in this range is generally enough to absorb new entrants to the labor force. It is not the kind of surge that signals overheating on its own.
segments.tr: - **165.000 là một con số vững chắc, không phải là ngoạn mục.** Trong một nền kinh tế đang phát triển, mức tăng trong khoảng này nhìn chung là đủ để hấp thụ những người mới gia nhập lực lượng lao động. Đây không phải là kiểu bùng nổ báo hiệu sự quá nhiệt tự thân của nó.

segments.src: - **4.1% is historically low.** By long-run standards, an unemployment rate near 4% is consistent with a tight labor market, where employers compete for workers.
segments.tr: - **4,1% là mức thấp trong lịch sử.** Theo tiêu chuẩn dài hạn, tỷ lệ thất nghiệp gần 4% phù hợp với thị trường lao động thắt chặt, nơi các nhà tuyển dụng cạnh tranh giành người lao động.

segments.src: - **Beating expectations matters in its own right.** Forecasters publish estimates before each report. A result above the consensus is treated as a surprise, and surprises move markets even when the underlying change is modest.
segments.tr: - **Việc đánh bại kỳ vọng tự bản thân nó rất quan trọng.** Các nhà dự báo công bố ước tính trước mỗi báo cáo. Kết quả vượt mức đồng thuận được coi là một bất ngờ, và những bất ngờ làm chuyển động thị trường ngay cả khi sự thay đổi cơ bản là khiêm tốn.

segments.src: - **Numbers get revised.** Initial estimates are often adjusted in later months. One report is a snapshot, not a verdict.
segments.tr: - **Các con số được điều chỉnh.** Các ước tính ban đầu thường được điều chỉnh vào những tháng sau đó. Một báo cáo là một bức ảnh chụp nhanh, không phải là một phán quyết.

segments.src: ## Where hiring was strong, and where it wasn't
segments.tr: ## Nơi tuyển dụng mạnh mẽ, và nơi không mạnh

segments.src: A headline total can hide very different experiences underneath.
segments.tr: Tổng số tiêu đề có thể ẩn giấu những trải nghiệm rất khác nhau bên dưới.

segments.src: In reports like this one, job gains tend to cluster in a small number of sectors, while others stay flat or shrink.
segments.tr: Trong các báo cáo như thế này, việc tăng trưởng việc làm có xu hướng tập trung ở một số ít lĩnh vực, trong khi các lĩnh vực khác vẫn đi ngang hoặc thu hẹp.

segments.src: **Industries.** Health care, social assistance, and government have been consistent sources of job growth in recent years, partly because demand for those services is steady and less sensitive to the business cycle.
segments.tr: **Các ngành công nghiệp.** Y tế, trợ giúp xã hội và chính phủ là những nguồn tăng trưởng việc làm ổn định trong những năm gần đây, một phần vì nhu cầu đối với các dịch vụ đó ổn định và ít nhạy cảm hơn với chu kỳ kinh doanh.

segments.src: Sectors that depend more on discretionary spending or interest rates, such as parts of manufacturing, construction, retail, and information technology, have tended to be more volatile.
segments.tr: Các lĩnh vực phụ thuộc nhiều hơn vào chi tiêu tùy ý hoặc lãi suất, chẳng hạn như một phần của sản xuất, xây dựng, bán lẻ và công nghệ thông tin, thường có xu hướng biến động mạnh hơn.

segments.src: When most of the gains come from a few areas, a strong total can coexist with real weakness elsewhere.
segments.tr: Khi phần lớn mức tăng đến từ một vài lĩnh vực, tổng số mạnh mẽ có thể cùng tồn tại với điểm yếu thực sự ở nơi khác.

segments.src: **Age groups.** Workers in their prime working years, roughly 25 to 54, have had very high employment rates.
segments.tr: **Nhóm tuổi.** Người lao động trong độ tuổi lao động chính, khoảng từ 25 đến 54 tuổi, có tỷ lệ việc làm rất cao.

segments.src: Younger workers and new graduates often face a harder search when employers slow hiring for entry-level roles.
segments.tr: Người lao động trẻ tuổi và sinh viên mới tốt nghiệp thường gặp nhiều khó khăn hơn trong việc tìm kiếm khi các nhà tuyển dụng làm chậm việc tuyển dụng cho các vai trò cấp thấp.

segments.src: Older workers who lose a job may take longer to find a new one.
segments.tr: Người lao động lớn tuổi bị mất việc có thể mất nhiều thời gian hơn để tìm việc mới.

segments.src: The overall unemployment rate averages all of this out, which is why a good headline can feel out of step with what some job seekers report.
segments.tr: Tỷ lệ thất nghiệp tổng thể làm phẳng tất cả những điều này, đó là lý do tại sao một tiêu đề tốt có thể cảm thấy không đồng điệu với những gì một số người tìm việc báo cáo.

segments.src: **Hours and job quality.** The count of jobs does not show whether positions are full-time, part-time, or temporary.
segments.tr: **Giờ làm việc và chất lượng công việc.** Số lượng việc làm không cho thấy liệu các vị trí là toàn thời gian, bán thời gian hay tạm thời.

segments.src: Analysts also look at average weekly hours and at the share of people working part-time who would prefer full-time work.
segments.tr: Các nhà phân tích cũng xem xét số giờ làm việc trung bình hàng tuần và tỷ lệ những người làm việc bán thời gian nhưng thích làm việc toàn thời gian.

segments.src: ## Wages: growing, but is it enough?
segments.tr: ## Tiền lương: đang tăng trưởng, nhưng liệu đã đủ chưa?

segments.src: Pay is the second half of the story.
segments.tr: Tiền lương là nửa thứ hai của câu chuyện.

segments.src: When unemployment is low, employers usually have to offer more to attract and keep workers, so wage growth tends to stay firm.
segments.tr: Khi thất nghiệp thấp, các nhà tuyển dụng thường phải trả lương cao hơn để thu hút và giữ chân người lao động, vì vậy tăng trưởng tiền lương có xu hướng duy trì vững chắc.

segments.src: That is good news for workers if pay rises faster than prices.
segments.tr: Đó là tin tốt cho người lao động nếu tiền lương tăng nhanh hơn giá cả.

segments.src: It is more complicated if inflation has also been running above the central bank's 2% goal.
segments.tr: Mọi chuyện phức tạp hơn nếu lạm phát cũng vượt mức mục tiêu 2% của ngân hàng trung ương.

segments.src: In that case, solid wage growth can look like a risk to policymakers.
segments.tr: Trong trường hợp đó, tăng trưởng tiền lương vững chắc có thể trông giống như một rủi ro đối với các nhà hoạch định chính sách.

segments.src: Their concern is that higher labor costs get passed on through prices, especially in service industries where labor is a large share of the bill.
segments.tr: Mối quan tâm của họ là chi phí lao động cao hơn được chuyển qua giá cả, đặc biệt là trong các ngành dịch vụ nơi lao động chiếm tỷ lớn trong hóa đơn.

segments.src: Averages also hide differences.
segments.tr: Các mức trung bình cũng che giấu sự khác biệt.

segments.src: Workers who change jobs have often received larger raises than those who stay put, while pay increases for people in the same role have been smaller.
segments.tr: Những người lao động thay đổi công việc thường nhận được mức tăng lương lớn hơn những người ở lại, trong khi việc tăng lương cho những người ở cùng một vị trí thì nhỏ hơn.

segments.src: Households that carry high rent, mortgage, or credit card costs may still feel stretched even when the national wage figure looks healthy.
segments.tr: Các hộ gia đình gánh nặng tiền thuê nhà, thế chấp hoặc thẻ tín dụng cao vẫn có thể cảm thấy căng thẳng ngay cả khi con số tiền lương quốc gia trông có vẻ lành mạnh.

segments.src: ## Job-switching: a sign of confidence, or a fading one
segments.tr: ## Chuyển đổi công việc: dấu hiệu của sự tự tin, hay sự phai nhạt

segments.src: Economists watch how often workers quit voluntarily.
segments.tr: Các nhà kinh tế theo dõi tần suất người lao động tự nguyện nghỉ việc.

segments.src: People generally leave a job when they are confident they can find a better one.
segments.tr: Mọi người thường rời bỏ công việc khi họ tự tin rằng mình có thể tìm được công việc tốt hơn.

segments.src: A high quit rate suggests a confident labor market with plenty of openings.
segments.tr: Tỷ lệ nghỉ việc cao cho thấy một thị trường lao động tự tin với nhiều vị trí trống.

segments.src: A falling quit rate suggests workers are staying put, and that employers are posting fewer openings.
segments.tr: Tỷ lệ nghỉ việc giảm cho thấy người lao động đang ở lại và các nhà tuyển dụng đang đăng ít vị trí trống hơn.

segments.src: In the past few years, the pace of job-switching has cooled from its peak.
segments.tr: Trong vài năm qua, tốc độ chuyển đổi công việc đã hạ nhiệt so với mức đỉnh.

segments.src: That has two effects:
segments.tr: Điều đó có hai tác động:

segments.src: - **Less pressure on pay.** When fewer people change jobs, employers feel less need to raise wages to compete.
segments.tr: - **Ít áp lực hơn đối với tiền lương.** Khi ít người thay đổi công việc hơn, các nhà tuyển dụng cảm thấy ít cần phải tăng lương để cạnh tranh.

segments.src: - **Harder entry for new job seekers.** Fewer vacancies are created when current employees stay in their roles, which can make it tougher for the unemployed and for people entering the workforce.
segments.tr: - **Lối vào khó khăn hơn cho những người tìm việc mới.** Ít vị trí tuyển dụng được tạo ra hơn khi nhân viên hiện tại ở lại vị trí của họ, điều này có thể làm cho việc tìm việc trở nên khó khăn hơn đối với những người thất nghiệp và những người gia nhập lực lượng lao động.

segments.src: This helps explain why a strong payroll number and a feeling of "a low-hire, low-fire" job market can both be true at once.
segments.tr: Điều này giúp giải thích tại sao một con số việc làm mạnh mẽ và cảm giác về một thị trường lao động "tuyển dụng ít, sa thải ít" có thể đều đúng cùng một lúc.

segments.src: ## Why markets read good news as a rate risk
segments.tr: ## Tại sao thị trường coi tin tốt là rủi ro lãi suất

segments.src: For many people, the most puzzling part of a jobs report day is that stocks or bonds sometimes fall after good news.
segments.tr: Đối với nhiều người, phần khó hiểu nhất của ngày báo cáo việc làm là cổ phiếu hoặc trái phiếu đôi khi giảm giá sau tin tốt.

segments.src: The reason is interest rates.
segments.tr: Lý do là lãi suất.

segments.src: The Federal Reserve sets its policy rate with two goals in mind: maximum employment and stable prices.
segments.tr: Cục Dự trữ Liên bang đặt ra lãi suất chính sách của mình với hai mục tiêu trong tâm trí: tối đa hóa việc làm và ổn định giá cả.

segments.src: When the labor market is strong and wages are rising, the case for lowering rates weakens.
segments.tr: Khi thị trường lao động mạnh và tiền lương đang tăng, lý lẽ cho việc hạ lãi suất sẽ suy yếu.

segments.src: Investors who had been counting on rate cuts may have to change their expectations.
segments.tr: Các nhà đầu tư từng tính toán việc cắt giảm lãi suất có thể phải thay đổi kỳ vọng của họ.

segments.src: Here is how that chain usually works:
segments.tr: Đây là cách chuỗi đó thường hoạt động:

segments.src: 1. **A stronger-than-expected report** suggests the economy does not need extra support from lower rates.
segments.tr: 1. **Một báo cáo mạnh hơn dự kiến** cho thấy nền kinh tế không cần sự hỗ trợ bổ sung từ lãi suất thấp hơn.

segments.src: 2. **Expectations for rate cuts are pushed back** or reduced.
segments.tr: 2. **Kỳ vọng cắt giảm lãi suất bị đẩy lùi** hoặc giảm bớt.

segments.src: 3. **Government bond yields often rise**, because investors now expect rates to stay higher for longer.
segments.tr: 3. **Lợi suất trái phiếu chính phủ thường tăng**, bởi vì các nhà đầu tư hiện kỳ vọng lãi suất sẽ duy trì ở mức cao hơn trong thời gian dài hơn.

segments.src: 4. **Higher yields can weigh on stock prices**, particularly for companies that rely on borrowing or whose value depends heavily on future earnings.
segments.tr: 4. **Lợi suất cao hơn có thể gây sức ép lên giá cổ phiếu**, đặc biệt là đối với các công ty phụ thuộc vào việc đi vay hoặc có giá trị phụ thuộc nhiều vào thu nhập trong tương lai.

segments.src: 5. **Borrowing costs for households stay elevated.** Mortgage rates, auto loans, and credit cards tend to follow broader rate expectations.
segments.tr: 5. **Chi phí đi vay của các hộ gia đình vẫn duy trì ở mức cao.** Lãi suất thế chấp, cho vay ô tô và thẻ tín dụng có xu hướng đi theo các kỳ vọng lãi suất rộng hơn.

segments.src: This is why a report can be good for workers and still unwelcome for people hoping for cheaper loans.
segments.tr: Đây là lý do tại sao một báo cáo có thể tốt cho người lao động nhưng vẫn không được hoan nghênh đối với những người hy vọng có các khoản vay rẻ hơn.

segments.src: It also explains why traders often react more to the difference between actual and expected numbers than to the numbers themselves.
segments.tr: Nó cũng giải thích tại sao các nhà giao dịch thường phản ứng nhiều hơn với sự khác biệt giữa các con số thực tế và dự kiến hơn là bản thân các con số.

segments.src: ## What to watch next
segments.tr: ## Những gì cần theo dõi tiếp theo

segments.src: A single month rarely changes the broader direction.
segments.tr: Một tháng duy nhất hiếm khi thay đổi định hướng rộng lớn hơn.

segments.src: These indicators give a fuller view:
segments.tr: Những chỉ báo này cung cấp một cái nhìn đầy đủ hơn:

segments.src: - **Revisions to prior months**, which can change the story of how strong hiring really was.
segments.tr: - **Các điều chỉnh đối với các tháng trước**, điều này có thể thay đổi câu chuyện về việc tuyển dụng thực sự mạnh mẽ đến mức nào.

segments.src: - **Average hourly earnings**, to see whether wage growth is speeding up or slowing down.
segments.tr: - **Thu nhập bình quân theo giờ**, để xem liệu tăng trưởng tiền lương đang tăng tốc hay chậm lại.

segments.src: - **The labor force participation rate**, which shows whether more people are coming back to look for work.
segments.tr: - **Tỷ lệ tham gia lực lượng lao động**, cho thấy liệu có nhiều người quay trở lại tìm việc hay không.

segments.src: - **Job openings and quit rates**, from the monthly JOLTS survey, for a read on employer demand and worker confidence.
segments.tr: - **Việc làm trống và tỷ lệ nghỉ việc**, từ cuộc khảo sát JOLTS hàng tháng, để đọc về nhu cầu của nhà tuyển dụng và sự tự tin của người lao động.

segments.src: - **Weekly jobless claims**, an early signal of layoffs.
segments.tr: - **Đơn xin trợ cấp thất nghiệp hàng tuần**, một tín hiệu sớm về việc sa thải nhân viên.

segments.src: - **Inflation data and Federal Reserve communications**, since these shape how policymakers respond to the labor market.
segments.tr: - **Dữ liệu lạm phát và thông tin liên lạc của Cục Dự trữ Liên bang**, vì những yếu tố này định hình cách các nhà hoạch định chính sách phản ứng với thị trường lao động.

segments.src: ## The bottom line
segments.tr: ## Điểm mấu chốt

segments.src: A report showing 165,000 new jobs and a 4.1% unemployment rate is, by most measures, evidence of a resilient labor market.
segments.tr: Một báo cáo cho thấy 165.000 việc làm mới và tỷ lệ thất nghiệp 4,1% là, theo hầu hết các thước đo, bằng chứng về một thị trường lao động kiên cường.

segments.src: But resilience is not the same as broad-based strength.
segments.tr: Nhưng sự kiên cường không giống như sức mạnh trên diện rộng.

segments.src: Gains concentrated in a few industries, uneven results across age groups, and slower job-switching all suggest that many people are not feeling the benefit equally.
segments.tr: Mức tăng tập trung ở một số ít ngành, kết quả không đồng đều giữa các nhóm tuổi và việc chuyển đổi công việc chậm hơn đều cho thấy rằng nhiều người không cảm nhận được lợi ích một cách công bằng.

segments.src: And because strong employment can delay interest rate cuts, good news for the job market can mean a more cautious outlook for borrowers and investors.
segments.tr: Và bởi vì việc làm mạnh mẽ có thể trì hoãn việc cắt giảm lãi suất, tin tốt cho thị trường việc làm có thể đồng nghĩa với một triển vọng thận trọng hơn đối với người đi vay và nhà đầu tư.

segments.src: The most useful way to read a jobs report is to look past the headline: ask who is being hired, how much they are paid, and what it means for the path of interest rates.
segments.tr: Cách hữu ích nhất để đọc báo cáo việc làm là nhìn xa hơn tiêu đề: hỏi xem ai đang được tuyển dụng, họ được trả bao nhiêu và điều đó có ý nghĩa gì đối với con đường lãi suất.
